4736.text: "I will also make it a possession for the porcupine, and pools of water. I will sweep it with the broom of destruction," says the Lord of hosts.

4737.text: The Lord of hosts has sworn, saying, "Surely, as I have thought, so shall it happen; and as I have purposed, so shall it stand:

4738.text: that I will break the Assyrian in my land, and tread him under foot on my mountains. Then his yoke will leave them, and his burden leave their shoulders.

4739.text: This is the plan that is determined for the whole earth. This is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.

4740.text: For the Lord of hosts has planned, and who can stop it? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?"

4741.text: This burden was in the year that king Ahaz died.

4742.text: Do not rejoice, O Philistia, all of you, because the rod that struck you is broken; for out of the serpent's root an adder will emerge, and his fruit will be a fiery flying serpent.

4743.text: The firstborn of the poor will eat, and the needy will lie down in safety; and I will kill your root with famine, and your remnant will be killed.

4744.text: Howl, gate! Cry, city! You are melted away, Philistia, all of you; for smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks.

4745.text: What will they answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people will take refuge.

4746.text: The burden of Moab: for in a night, Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing; for in a night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing.

4747.text: They have gone up to Bayith, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba. Baldness is on all of their heads. Every beard is cut off.

4748.text: In their streets, they dress themselves in sackcloth. In their streets and on their housetops, everyone wails, weeping abundantly.

4749.text: Heshbon cries out with Elealeh. Their voice is heard even to Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud. Their souls tremble within them.

4750.text: My heart cries out for Moab! Her Nazirites flee to Zoar, to Eglath Shelishiyah; for they go up by the ascent of Luhith with weeping; for in the way of Horonaim, they raise up a cry of destruction.

4751.text: For the waters of Nimrim will be desolate; for the grass has withered away, the tender grass fails, there is no green thing.

4752.text: Therefore they will carry away the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have stored up, over the brook of the willows.

4753.text: For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab; its wailing to Eglaim, and its wailing to Beer Elim.

4754.text: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring yet more on Dimon, a lion on those of Moab who escape, and on the remnant of the land.

4755.text: Send the lambs for the ruler of the land from Selah to the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.

4756.text: For it will be that as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.

4757.text: Give counsel! Execute justice! Make your shade like the night in the midst of the noonday! Hide the outcasts! Do not betray the fugitive!

4758.text: Let my outcasts dwell with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortioner is brought to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.

4759.text: A throne will be established in loving kindness. One will sit on it in truth, in the tent of David, judging, seeking justice, and swift to do righteousness.

4760.text: We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud; even of his arrogance, his pride, and his wrath. His boastings are nothing.

4761.text: Therefore Moab will wail for Moab. Everyone will wail. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, utterly stricken.

4762.text: For the fields of Heshbon languish with the vine of Sibmah. The lords of the nations have broken down its choice branches, which reached even to Jazer, which wandered into the wilderness. Its shoots were spread abroad. They passed over the sea.

4763.text: Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah. I will water you with my tears, Heshbon, and Elealeh: for on your summer fruits and on your harvest the battle shout has fallen.

4764.text: Gladness is taken away, and joy out of the fruitful field; and in the vineyards there will be no singing, neither joyful noise. Nobody will tread out wine in the presses. I have made the shouting stop.

4765.text: Therefore my heart sounds like a harp for Moab, and my inward parts for Kir Heres.

4766.text: It will happen that when Moab presents himself, when he wearies himself on the high place, and comes to his sanctuary to pray, that he will not prevail.

4767.text: This is the word that the Lord spoke concerning Moab in time past.

4768.text: But now the Lord has spoken, saying, "Within three years, as a worker bound by contract would count them, the glory of Moab shall be brought into contempt, with all his great multitude; and the remnant will be very small and feeble."

4769.text: The burden of Damascus: "Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it will be a ruinous heap.

4770.text: The cities of Aroer are forsaken. They will be for flocks, which shall lie down, and none shall make them afraid.

4771.text: The fortress shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria. They will be as the glory of the children of Israel," says the Lord of hosts.

4772.text: "It will happen in that day that the glory of Jacob will be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh will become lean.

4773.text: It will be like when the harvester gathers the wheat, and his arm reaps the grain. Yes, it will be like when one gleans grain in the valley of Rephaim.

4774.text: Yet gleanings will be left there, like the shaking of an olive tree, two or three olives in the top of the uppermost bough, four or five in the outermost branches of a fruitful tree," says the Lord, the God of Israel.

4775.text: In that day, people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will have respect for the Holy One of Israel.

4776.text: They will not look to the altars, the work of their hands; neither shall they respect that which their fingers have made, either the Asherim, or the incense altars.

4777.text: In that day, their strong cities will be like the forsaken places in the woods and on the mountain top, which were forsaken from before the children of Israel; and it will be a desolation.

4778.text: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation, and have not remembered the rock of your strength. Therefore you plant pleasant plants, and set out foreign seedlings.

4779.text: In the day of your planting, you hedge it in. In the morning, you make your seed blossom, but the harvest flees away in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.

4780.text: Ah, the uproar of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the seas; and the rushing of nations, that rush like the rushing of mighty waters!

4781.text: The nations will rush like the rushing of many waters: but he will rebuke them, and they will flee far off, and will be chased like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like the whirling dust before the storm.

4782.text: At evening, behold, terror! Before the morning, they are no more. This is the portion of those who plunder us, and the lot of those who rob us.

4783.text: Ah, the land of the rustling of wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia;

4784.text: that sends ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of papyrus on the waters, saying, "Go, you swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people awesome from their beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide!"

4785.text: All you inhabitants of the world, and you dwellers on the earth, when a banner is lifted up on the mountains, look! When the trumpet is blown, listen!

4786.text: For the Lord said to me, "I will be still, and I will see from my dwelling place, like the clear heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."

4787.text: For before the harvest, when the blossom is over, and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and he will cut down and take away the spreading branches.

4788.text: They will be left together for the ravenous birds of the mountains, and for the animals of the earth. The ravenous birds will summer on them, and all the animals of the earth will winter on them.

4789.text: In that time, a present will be brought to the Lord of hosts from a people tall and smooth, even from a people awesome from their beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of the Lord of hosts, Mount Zion.

4790.text: The burden of Egypt: "Behold, the Lord rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble at his presence; and the heart of Egypt will melt in its midst.

4791.text: I will stir up the Egyptians against the Egyptians, and they will fight everyone against his brother, and everyone against his neighbor; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.

4792.text: The spirit of Egypt will fail in its midst. I will destroy its counsel. They will seek the idols, the charmers, those who have familiar spirits, and the wizards.

4793.text: I will give over the Egyptians into the hand of a cruel lord. A fierce king will rule over them," says the Lord, the Lord of hosts.

4794.text: The waters will fail from the sea, and the river will be wasted and become dry.

4795.text: The rivers will become foul. The streams of Egypt will be diminished and dried up. The reeds and flags will wither away.

4796.text: The meadows by the Nile, by the brink of the Nile, and all the sown fields of the Nile, will become dry, be driven away, and be no more.

4797.text: The fishermen will lament, and all those who fish in the Nile will mourn, and those who spread nets on the waters will languish.

4798.text: Moreover those who work in combed flax, and those who weave white cloth, will be confounded.

4799.text: The pillars will be broken in pieces. All those who work for hire will be grieved in soul.

4800.text: The princes of Zoan are utterly foolish. The counsel of the wisest counselors of Pharaoh has become stupid. How do you say to Pharaoh, "I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?"

4801.text: Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you now; and let them know what the Lord of hosts has purposed concerning Egypt.

4802.text: The princes of Zoan have become fools. The princes of Memphis are deceived. They have caused Egypt to go astray, who are the cornerstone of her tribes.

4803.text: The Lord has mixed a spirit of perverseness in the midst of her; and they have caused Egypt to go astray in all of its works, like a drunken man staggers in his vomit.

4804.text: Neither shall there be for Egypt any work, which head or tail, palm branch or rush, may do.

4805.text: In that day the Egyptians will be like women. They will tremble and fear because of the shaking of the hand of the Lord of hosts, which he shakes over them.

4806.text: The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt. Everyone to whom mention is made of it will be afraid, because of the plans of the Lord of hosts, which he determines against it.

4807.text: In that day, there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan, and swear loyalty to the Lord of hosts. One will be called "The City of the Sun."

4808.text: In that day, there will be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the Lord at its border.

4809.text: It will be for a sign and for a witness to the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt; for they will cry to the Lord because of oppressors, and he will send them a savior and a defender, and he will deliver them.

4810.text: The Lord will be known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know the Lord in that day. Yes, they will worship with sacrifice and offering, and will make vows to the Lord, and will perform them.

4811.text: The Lord will strike Egypt, striking and healing. They will return to the Lord, and he will listen to their pleas, and will heal them.

4812.text: In that day there will be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and the Assyrian shall come into Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria; and the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians.

4813.text: In that day, Israel will be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth;

4814.text: because the Lord of hosts has blessed them, saying, "Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance."

4815.text: In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and took it;

4816.text: at that time the Lord spoke by Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, "Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your shoes from off your feet." He did so, walking naked and barefoot.

4817.text: The Lord said, "As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a wonder concerning Egypt and concerning Ethiopia,

4818.text: so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, and with buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.

4819.text: They will be dismayed and confounded, because of Ethiopia their expectation, and of Egypt their glory.

4820.text: The inhabitants of this coast land will say in that day, 'Behold, this is our expectation, where we fled for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria. And we, how will we escape?'"

4821.text: The oracle of the wilderness of the sea. As whirlwinds in the Negev sweep through, it comes from the wilderness, from an awesome land.

4822.text: A grievous vision is declared to me. The treacherous man deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam; attack! I have stopped all of Media's sighing.

4823.text: Therefore my thighs are filled with anguish. Pains have taken hold on me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am in so much pain that I can't hear. I so am dismayed that I can't see.

4824.text: My heart flutters. Horror has frightened me. The twilight that I desired has been turned into trembling for me.

4825.text: They prepare the table. They set the watch. They eat. They drink. Rise up, you princes, oil the shield!

4826.text: For the Lord said to me, "Go, set a watchman. Let him declare what he sees.

4827.text: When he sees a troop, horsemen in pairs, a troop of donkeys, a troop of camels, he shall listen diligently with great attentiveness."

4828.text: He cried like a lion: "Lord, I stand continually on the watchtower in the daytime, and every night I stay at my post.

4829.text: Behold, here comes a troop of men, horsemen in pairs." He answered, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the engraved images of her gods are broken to the ground.

4830.text: You are my threshing, and the grain of my floor!" That which I have heard from the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.

4831.text: The burden of Dumah. One calls to me out of Seir, "Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?"

4832.text: The watchman said, "The morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire. Come back again."

4833.text: The burden on Arabia. In the forest in Arabia you will lodge, you caravans of Dedanites.

4834.text: They brought water to him who was thirsty. The inhabitants of the land of Tema met the fugitives with their bread.

4835.text: For they fled away from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.

4836.text: For the Lord said to me, "Within a year, as a worker bound by contract would count it, all the glory of Kedar will fail,

4837.text: and the residue of the number of the archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, will be few; for the Lord, the God of Israel, has spoken it."

4838.text: The burden of the valley of vision. What ails you now, that you have all gone up to the housetops?

4839.text: You that are full of shouting, a tumultuous city, a joyous town; your slain are not slain with the sword, neither are they dead in battle.

4840.text: All your rulers fled away together. They were bound by the archers. All who were found by you were bound together. They fled far away.

4841.text: Therefore I said, "Look away from me. I will weep bitterly. Do not labor to comfort me for the destruction of the daughter of my people.

4842.text: For it is a day of confusion, and of treading down, and of perplexity, from the Lord, the Lord of hosts, in the valley of vision; a breaking down of the walls, and a crying to the mountains."

4843.text: Elam carried his quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen; and Kir uncovered the shield.

4844.text: It happened that your choicest valleys were full of chariots, and the horsemen set themselves in array at the gate.

4845.text: He took away the covering of Judah; and you looked in that day to the armor in the house of the forest.

4846.text: You saw the breaches of the city of David, that they were many; and you gathered together the waters of the lower pool.

4847.text: You numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and you broke down the houses to fortify the wall.

4848.text: You also made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you did not look to him who had done this, neither did you have respect for him who purposed it long ago.

4849.text: In that day, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, called to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to dressing in sackcloth:

4850.text: and behold, joy and gladness, killing cattle and killing sheep, eating flesh and drinking wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die."

4851.text: The Lord of hosts revealed himself in my ears, "Surely this iniquity will not be forgiven you until you die," says the Lord, the Lord of hosts.

4852.text: Thus says the Lord, the Lord of hosts, "Go, get yourself to this treasurer, even to Shebna, who is over the house, and say,

4853.text: 'What are you doing here? Who has you here, that you have dug out a tomb here?' Cutting himself out a tomb on high, chiseling a habitation for himself in the rock!"

4854.text: Behold, the Lord will overcome you and hurl you away violently. Yes, he will grasp you firmly.

4855.text: He will surely wind you around and around, and throw you like a ball into a large country. There you will die, and there the chariots of your glory will be, you shame of your lord's house.

4856.text: I will thrust you from your office. You will be pulled down from your station.

4857.text: It will happen in that day that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah,

4858.text: and I will clothe him with your robe, and strengthen him with your belt. I will commit your government into his hand; and he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.

4859.text: I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder. He will open, and no one will shut. He will shut, and no one will open.

4860.text: I will fasten him like a nail in a sure place. He will be for a throne of glory to his father's house.

4861.text: They will hang on him all the glory of his father's house, the offspring and the issue, every small vessel, from the cups even to all the pitchers.

4862.text: "In that day," says the Lord of hosts, "the nail that was fastened in a sure place will give way. It will be cut down, and fall. The burden that was on it will be cut off, for the Lord has spoken it."

4863.text: The burden of Tyre. Howl, you ships of Tarshish! For it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in. From the land of Kittim it is revealed to them.

4864.text: Be still, you inhabitants of the coast, you whom the merchants of Sidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished.

4865.text: On great waters, the seed of the Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue. She was the market of nations.

4866.text: Be ashamed, Sidon; for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying, "I have not travailed, nor brought forth, neither have I nourished young men, nor brought up virgins."

4867.text: When the report comes to Egypt, they will be in anguish at the report of Tyre.

4868.text: Pass over to Tarshish! Wail, you inhabitants of the coast!

4869.text: Is this your joyous city, whose antiquity is of ancient days, whose feet carried her far away to travel?

4870.text: Who has planned this against Tyre, the giver of crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honorable of the earth?

4871.text: The Lord of hosts has planned it, to stain the pride of all glory, to bring into contempt all the honorable of the earth.

4872.text: Pass through your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish. There is no restraint any more.

4873.text: He has stretched out his hand over the sea. He has shaken the kingdoms. The Lord has ordered the destruction of Canaan's strongholds.

4874.text: He said, "You shall rejoice no more, you oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon. Arise, pass over to Kittim. Even there you will have no rest."

4875.text: Behold, the land of the Chaldeans. This people was not. The Assyrians founded it for those who dwell in the wilderness. They set up their towers. They overthrew its palaces. They made it a ruin.

4876.text: Howl, you ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is laid waste!

4877.text: It will come to pass in that day that Tyre will be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king. After the end of seventy years it will be to Tyre like in the song of the prostitute.

4878.text: Take a harp; go about the city, you prostitute that has been forgotten. Make sweet melody. Sing many songs, that you may be remembered.

4879.text: It will happen after the end of seventy years that the Lord will visit Tyre, and she shall return to her wages, and will play the prostitute with all the kingdoms of the world on the surface of the earth.

4880.text: Her merchandise and her wages will be holiness to the Lord. It will not be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise will be for those who dwell before the Lord, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing.

4881.text: Behold, the Lord makes the earth empty, makes it waste, turns it upside down, and scatters its inhabitants.

4882.text: It will be as with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the creditor, so with the debtor; as with the taker of interest, so with the giver of interest.

4883.text: The earth will be utterly emptied and utterly laid waste; for the Lord has spoken this word.

4884.text: The earth mourns and fades away. The world languishes and fades away. The lofty people of the earth languish.

4885.text: The earth also is polluted under its inhabitants, because they have transgressed the laws, violated the statutes, and broken the everlasting covenant.

4886.text: Therefore the curse has devoured the earth, and those who dwell therein are found guilty. Therefore the inhabitants of the earth are burned, and few men left.

4887.text: The new wine mourns. The vine languishes. All the merry-hearted sigh.

4888.text: The mirth of tambourines ceases. The sound of those who rejoice ends. The joy of the harp ceases.

4889.text: They will not drink wine with a song. Strong drink will be bitter to those who drink it.

4890.text: The confused city is broken down. Every house is shut up, that no man may come in.

4891.text: There is a crying in the streets because of the wine. All joy is darkened. The mirth of the land is gone.

4892.text: The city is left in desolation, and the gate is struck with destruction.

4893.text: For it will be so in the midst of the earth among the peoples, as the shaking of an olive tree, as the gleanings when the vintage is done.

4894.text: These shall lift up their voice. They will shout for the majesty of the Lord. They cry aloud from the sea.

4895.text: Therefore glorify the Lord in the east, even the name of the Lord, the God of Israel, in the islands of the sea!

4896.text: From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs. Glory to the righteous! But I said, "I pine away! I pine away! Woe is me!" The treacherous have dealt treacherously. Yes, the treacherous have dealt very treacherously.

4897.text: Fear, the pit, and the snare, are on you who inhabitant the earth.

4898.text: It will happen that he who flees from the noise of the fear will fall into the pit; and he who comes up out of the midst of the pit will be taken in the snare; for the windows on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth tremble.

4899.text: The earth is utterly broken. The earth is torn apart. The earth is shaken violently.

4900.text: The earth will stagger like a drunken man, and will sway back and forth like a hammock. Its disobedience will be heavy on it, and it will fall and not rise again.

4901.text: It shall happen in that day that the Lord will punish the army of the high ones on high, and the kings of the earth on the earth.

4902.text: They shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison; and after many days shall they be visited.

4903.text: Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed; for the Lord of hosts will reign on Mount Zion, and in Jerusalem; and before his elders will be glory.

4904.text: The Lord, you are my God. I will exalt you! I will praise your name, for you have done wonderful things, things planned long ago, in complete faithfulness and truth.

4905.text: For you have made a city into a heap, a fortified city into a ruin, a palace of strangers to be no city. It will never be built.

4906.text: Therefore a strong people will glorify you. A city of awesome nations will fear you.

4907.text: For you have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the dreaded ones is like a storm against the wall.

4908.text: As the heat in a dry place will you bring down the noise of strangers; as the heat by the shade of a cloud, the song of the dreaded ones will be brought low.

4909.text: In this mountain, the Lord of hosts will make all peoples a feast of fat things, a feast of choice wines, of fat things full of marrow, of well refined choice wines.

4910.text: He will destroy in this mountain the surface of the covering that covers all peoples, and the veil that is spread over all nations.

4911.text: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord God will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for the Lord has spoken it.

4912.text: It shall be said in that day, "Behold, this is our God! We have waited for him, and he will save us! This is the Lord! We have waited for him. We will be glad and rejoice in his salvation!"

4913.text: For in this mountain the hand of the Lord will rest. Moab will be trodden down in his place, even like straw is trodden down in the water of the dunghill.

4914.text: He will spread out his hands in its midst, like one who swims spreads out hands to swim, but his pride will be humbled together with the craft of his hands.

4915.text: He has brought the high fortress of your walls down, laid low, and brought to the ground, even to the dust.

4916.text: In that day, this song will be sung in the land of Judah: "We have a strong city. He appoints salvation for walls and ramparts.

4917.text: Open the gates, that the righteous nation may enter: the one which keeps faith.

4918.text: You will keep whoever's mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.

4919.text: Trust in the Lord forever; for in Yah, the Lord, is an everlasting Rock.

4920.text: For he has brought down those who dwell on high, the lofty city. He lays it low. He lays it low even to the ground. He brings it even to the dust.

4921.text: The foot shall tread it down; Even the feet of the poor, and the steps of the needy."

4922.text: The way of the just is uprightness. You who are upright make the path of the righteous level.

4923.text: Yes, in the way of your judgments, the Lord, have we waited for you. Your name and your renown are the desire of our soul.

4924.text: With my soul have I desired you in the night. Yes, with my spirit within me will I seek you earnestly; for when your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.

4925.text: Let favor be shown to the wicked, yet he will not learn righteousness. In the land of uprightness he will deal wrongfully, and will not see the Lord's majesty.

4926.text: The Lord, your hand is lifted up, yet they do not see; but they will see your zeal for the people, and be disappointed. Yes, fire will consume your adversaries.

4927.text: The Lord, you will ordain peace for us, for you have also worked all our works for us.

4928.text: The Lord our God, other lords besides you have had dominion over us, but by you only will we make mention of your name.

4929.text: The dead shall not live. The deceased shall not rise. Therefore have you visited and destroyed them, and caused all memory of them to perish.

4930.text: You have increased the nation, O Lord. You have increased the nation! You are glorified! You have enlarged all the borders of the land.

4931.text: Lord, in trouble they have visited you. They poured out a prayer when your chastening was on them.

4932.text: Like as a woman with child, who draws near the time of her delivery, is in pain and cries out in her pangs; so we have been before you, Lord.

4933.text: We have been with child. We have been in pain. We gave birth, it seems, only to wind. We have not worked any deliverance in the earth; neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen.

4934.text: Your dead shall live. My dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast forth the dead.

4935.text: Come, my people, enter into your chambers, and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation is past.

4936.text: For, behold, the Lord comes forth out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. The earth also will disclose her blood, and will no longer cover her slain.

4937.text: In that day, the Lord with his hard and great and strong sword will punish leviathan, the fleeing serpent, and leviathan the twisted serpent; and he will kill the dragon that is in the sea.

4938.text: In that day, sing to her, "A pleasant vineyard!

4939.text: I, the Lord, am its keeper. I will water it every moment. Lest anyone damage it, I will keep it night and day.

4940.text: Wrath is not in me, but if I should find briers and thorns, I would do battle! I would march on them and I would burn them together.

4941.text: Or else let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me. Let him make peace with me."

4942.text: In days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will blossom and bud. They will fill the surface of the world with fruit.

4943.text: Has he struck them as he struck those who struck them? Or are they killed like those who killed them were killed?

4944.text: In measure, when you send them away, you contend with them. He has removed them with his rough blast in the day of the east wind.

4945.text: Therefore, by this the iniquity of Jacob will be forgiven, and this is all the fruit of taking away his sin: that he makes all the stones of the altar as chalk stones that are beaten in pieces, so that the Asherim and the incense altars shall rise no more.

4946.text: For the fortified city is solitary, a habitation deserted and forsaken, like the wilderness. The calf will feed there, and there he will lie down, and consume its branches.

4947.text: When its boughs are withered, they will be broken off. The women will come and set them on fire, for they are a people of no understanding. Therefore he who made them will not have compassion on them, and he who formed them will show them no favor.

4948.text: It will happen in that day, that the Lord will thresh from the flowing stream of the Euphrates to the brook of Egypt; and you will be gathered one by one, children of Israel.

4949.text: It will happen in that day that a great trumpet will be blown; and those who were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and those who were outcasts in the land of Egypt, shall come; and they will worship the Lord in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.

4950.text: Woe to the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley of those who are overcome with wine!

4951.text: Behold, the Lord has a mighty and strong one. Like a storm of hail, a destroying storm, and like a storm of mighty waters overflowing, he will cast them down to the earth with his hand.

4952.text: The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim will be trodden under foot.

4953.text: The fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley, shall be like the first-ripe fig before the summer; which someone picks and eats as soon as he sees it.

4954.text: In that day, the Lord of hosts will become a crown of glory, and a diadem of beauty, to the residue of his people;

4955.text: and a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, and strength to those who turn back the battle at the gate.

4956.text: They also reel with wine, and stagger with strong drink. The priest and the prophet reel with strong drink. They are swallowed up by wine. They stagger with strong drink. They err in vision. They stumble in judgment.

4957.text: For all tables are completely full of filthy vomit and filthiness.

4958.text: Whom will he teach knowledge? To whom will he explain the message? Those who are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts?

4959.text: For it is precept on precept, precept on precept; line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little.

4960.text: But he will speak to this nation with stammering lips and a strange language;

4961.text: to whom he said, "This is the resting place. Give rest to weary;" and "This is the refreshing;" yet they would not hear.

4962.text: Therefore the word of the Lord will be to them precept on precept, precept on precept; line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little; that they may go, fall backward, be broken, be snared, and be taken.

4963.text: Therefore hear the word of the Lord, you scoffers, that rule this people in Jerusalem:

4964.text: "Because you have said, 'We have made a covenant with death, and with Sheol are we in agreement. When the overflowing scourge passes through, it won't come to us; for we have made lies our refuge, and we have hidden ourselves under falsehood.'"

4965.text: Therefore thus says the Lord God, "Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. He who believes shall not be in fear.

4966.text: I will make justice the measuring line, and righteousness the plumb line. The hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters will overflow the hiding place.

4967.text: Your covenant with death shall be annulled, and your agreement with Sheol shall not stand. When the overflowing scourge passes through, then you will be trampled down by it.

4968.text: As often as it passes through, it will seize you; for morning by morning it will pass through, by day and by night; and it will be nothing but terror to understand the message."

4969.text: For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap oneself in.

4970.text: For the Lord will rise up as on Mount Perazim. He will be angry as in the valley of Gibeon; that he may do his work, his unusual work, and bring to pass his act, his extraordinary act.

4971.text: Now therefore do not be scoffers, lest your bonds be made strong; for I have heard a decree of destruction from the Lord, the Lord of hosts, on the whole earth.

4972.text: Give ear, and hear my voice! Listen, and hear my speech!

4973.text: Does he who plows to sow plow continually? Does he keep turning the soil and breaking the clods?

4974.text: When he has leveled its surface, doesn't he plant the dill, and scatter the cumin seed, and put in the wheat in rows, the barley in the appointed place, and the spelt in its place?

4975.text: For his God instructs him in right judgment, and teaches him.

4976.text: For the dill are not threshed with a sharp instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned over the cumin; but the dill is beaten out with a stick, and the cumin with a rod.

4977.text: Bread flour must be ground; so he will not always be threshing it. Although he drives the wheel of his threshing cart over it, his horses do not grind it.

4978.text: This also comes forth from the Lord of hosts, who is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in wisdom.

4979.text: Woe to Ariel! Ariel, the city where David encamped! Add year to year; let the feasts come around;

4980.text: then I will distress Ariel, and there will be mourning and lamentation. She shall be to me as an altar hearth.

4981.text: I will encamp against you all around you, and will lay siege against you with posted troops. I will raise siege works against you.

4982.text: You will be brought down, and will speak out of the ground. Your speech will mumble out of the dust. Your voice will be as of one who has a familiar spirit, out of the ground, and your speech will whisper out of the dust.

4983.text: But the multitude of your foes will be like fine dust, and the multitude of the ruthless ones like chaff that blows away. Yes, it will be in an instant, suddenly.

4984.text: She will be visited by the Lord of hosts with thunder, with earthquake, with great noise, with whirlwind and storm, and with the flame of a devouring fire.

4985.text: The multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel, even all who fight against her and her stronghold, and who distress her, will be like a dream, a vision of the night.

4986.text: It will be like when a hungry man dreams, and behold, he eats; but he awakes, and his hunger isn't satisfied; or like when a thirsty man dreams, and behold, he drinks; but he awakes, and behold, he is faint, and he is still thirsty. The multitude of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion will be like that.

4987.text: Pause and wonder! Blind yourselves and be blind! They are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.

4988.text: For the Lord has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep, and has closed your eyes (the prophets), and he has covered your heads (the seers).

4989.text: All vision has become to you like the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one who is educated, saying, "Read this, please;" and he says, "I can't, for it is sealed:"

4990.text: and the book is delivered to one who is not educated, saying, "Read this, please;" and he says, "I can't read."

4991.text: The Lord said, "Because this people draws near with their mouth and with their lips to honor me, but they have removed their heart far from me, but in vain do they worship me, teaching the commandments and doctrines of men.

4992.text: Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvelous work among this people, even a marvelous work and a wonder; and the wisdom of their wise men will perish, and the understanding of their prudent men will be hidden."

4993.text: Woe to those who deeply hide their counsel from the Lord, and whose works are in the dark, and who say, "Who sees us?" and "Who knows us?"

4994.text: You turn things upside down! Should the potter be thought to be like clay; that the thing made should say about him who made it, "He did not make me;" or the thing formed say of him who formed it, "He has no understanding?"

4995.text: Isn't it yet a very little while, and Lebanon will be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field will be regarded as a forest?

4996.text: In that day, the deaf will hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind will see out of obscurity and out of darkness.

4997.text: The humble also will increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

4998.text: For the ruthless is brought to nothing, and the scoffer ceases, and all those who are alert to do evil are cut off-

4999.text: who cause a person to be indicted by a word, and lay a snare for the arbiter in the gate, and who deprive the innocent of justice with false testimony.

5000.text: Therefore thus says the Lord, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob: "Jacob shall no longer be ashamed, neither shall his face grow pale.

5001.text: But when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in the midst of him, they will sanctify my name. Yes, they will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and will stand in awe of the God of Israel.

5002.text: They also who err in spirit will come to understanding, and those who grumble will receive instruction."

5003.text: "Woe to the rebellious children," says the Lord, "who take counsel, but not from me; and who make an alliance, but not with my Spirit, that they may add sin to sin,

5004.text: who set out to go down into Egypt, and have not asked my advice; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to take refuge in the shadow of Egypt!

5005.text: Therefore the strength of Pharaoh will be your shame, and the refuge in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.

5006.text: For their princes are at Zoan, and their ambassadors have come to Hanes.

5007.text: They shall all be ashamed because of a people that can't profit them, that are not a help nor profit, but a shame, and also a reproach."

5008.text: The oracle of the animals of the Negev. Through the land of trouble and anguish, of the lioness and the lion, the viper and fiery flying serpent, they carry their riches on the shoulders of young donkeys, and their treasures on the humps of camels, to an unprofitable people.

5009.text: For Egypt helps in vain, and to no purpose; therefore have I called her Rahab who sits still.

5010.text: Now go, write it before them on a tablet, and inscribe it in a book, that it may be for the time to come forever and ever.

5011.text: For it is a rebellious people, lying children, children who will not hear the law of the Lord;

5012.text: who tell the seers, "Do not see!" and to the prophets, "Do not prophesy to us right things. Tell us pleasant things. Prophesy deceits.

5013.text: Get out of the way. Turn aside from the path. Cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us."

5014.text: Therefore thus says the Holy One of Israel, "Because you despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and rely on it;

5015.text: therefore this iniquity shall be to you like a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking comes suddenly in an instant.

5016.text: He will break it as a potter's vessel is broken, breaking it in pieces without sparing, so that there won't be found among the broken piece a piece good enough to take fire from the hearth, or to dip up water out of the cistern."

5017.text: For thus said the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, "You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence." You refused,

5018.text: but you said, "No, for we will flee on horses;" therefore you will flee; and, "We will ride on the swift;" therefore those who pursue you will be swift.

5019.text: One thousand will flee at the threat of one. At the threat of five, you will flee until you are left like a beacon on the top of a mountain, and like a banner on a hill.

5020.text: Therefore the Lord will wait, that he may be gracious to you; and therefore he will be exalted, that he may have mercy on you, for the Lord is a God of justice. Blessed are all those who wait for him.

5021.text: For the people will dwell in Zion at Jerusalem. You will weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the voice of your cry. When he hears you, he will answer you.

5022.text: Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teachers won't be hidden anymore, but your eyes will see your teachers;

5023.text: and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, "This is the way. Walk in it."

5024.text: You shall defile the overlaying of your engraved images of silver, and the plating of your molten images of gold. You shall cast them away as an unclean thing. You shall tell it, "Go away!"

5025.text: He will give the rain for your seed, with which you will sow the ground; and bread of the increase of the ground will be rich and plentiful. In that day, your livestock will feed in large pastures.

5026.text: The oxen likewise and the young donkeys that till the ground will eat savory provender, which has been winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.

5027.text: There shall be brooks and streams of water on every lofty mountain and on every high hill in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

5028.text: Moreover the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord binds up the fracture of his people, and heals the wound they were struck with.

5029.text: Behold, the name of the Lord comes from far away, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke. His lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is as a devouring fire.

5030.text: His breath is as an overflowing stream that reaches even to the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction; and a bridle that leads to ruin will be in the jaws of the peoples.

5031.text: You will have a song, as in the night when a holy feast is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goes with a flute to come to the Lord's mountain, to Israel's Rock.

5032.text: The Lord will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the descent of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, storm, and hailstones.

5033.text: For through the voice of the Lord the Assyrian will be dismayed. He will strike him with his rod.

5034.text: Every stroke of the rod of punishment, which the Lord will lay on him, will be with the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight with them in battles, brandishing weapons.

5035.text: For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is made ready. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. The Lord's breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.

5036.text: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, but they do not look to the Holy One of Israel, and they do not seek the Lord!

5037.text: Yet he also is wise, and will bring disaster, and will not call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evildoers, and against the help of those who work iniquity.

5038.text: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the Lord stretches out his hand, both he who helps shall stumble, and he who is helped shall fall, and they all shall be consumed together.

5039.text: For thus says the Lord to me, "As the lion and the young lion growling over his prey, if a multitude of shepherds is called together against him, will not be dismayed at their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them, so the Lord of hosts will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its heights.

5040.text: As birds hovering, so the Lord of hosts will protect Jerusalem. He will protect and deliver it. He will pass over and preserve it."

5041.text: Return to him from whom you have deeply revolted, children of Israel.

5042.text: For in that day everyone shall cast away his idols of silver and his idols of gold-sin which your own hands have made for you.

5043.text: "The Assyrian will fall by the sword, not of man; and the sword, not of mankind, shall devour him. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will become subject to forced labor.

5044.text: His rock will pass away by reason of terror, and his princes will be afraid of the banner," says the Lord, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.

5045.text: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in justice.

5046.text: A man shall be as a hiding place from the wind, and a shelter from the storm, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a large rock in a weary land.

5047.text: The eyes of those who see will not be dim, and the ears of those who hear will listen.

5048.text: The heart of the rash will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers will be ready to speak plainly.

5049.text: The fool will no longer be called noble, nor the scoundrel be highly respected.

5050.text: For the fool will speak folly, and his heart will work iniquity, to practice profanity, and to utter error against the Lord, To make empty the soul of the hungry, and to cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.

5051.text: The ways of the scoundrel are evil. He devises wicked devices to destroy the humble with lying words, even when the needy speaks right.

5052.text: But the noble devises noble things; and he will continue in noble things.

5053.text: Rise up, you women who are at ease! Hear my voice! You careless daughters, give ear to my speech!

5054.text: For days beyond a year you will be troubled, you careless women; for the vintage shall fail. The harvest won't come.

5055.text: Tremble, you women who are at ease! Be troubled, you careless ones! Strip yourselves, make yourselves naked, and put sackcloth on your waist.

5056.text: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.

5057.text: Thorns and briars will come up on my people's land; yes, on all the houses of joy in the joyous city.

5058.text: For the palace will be forsaken. The populous city will be deserted. The hill and the watchtower will be for dens forever, a delight for wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks;

5059.text: Until the Spirit is poured on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is considered a forest.

5060.text: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness; and righteousness will remain in the fruitful field.

5061.text: The work of righteousness will be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.

5062.text: My people will abide in a peaceful habitation, in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting places.

5063.text: Though hail flattens the forest, and the city is leveled completely.

5064.text: Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, who send out the feet of the ox and the donkey.

5065.text: Woe to you who destroy, but you weren't destroyed; and who betray, but nobody betrayed you! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; and when you have made an end of betrayal, you will be betrayed.

5066.text: Lord, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.

5067.text: At the noise of the thunder, the peoples have fled. When you lift yourself up, the nations are scattered.

5068.text: Your spoil will be gathered as the caterpillar gathers. Men will leap on it as locusts leap.

5069.text: The Lord is exalted, for he dwells on high. He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.

5070.text: There will be stability in your times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the Lord is your treasure.

5071.text: Behold, their valiant ones cry outside; the ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.

5072.text: The highways are desolate. The traveling man ceases. The covenant is broken. He has despised the cities. He doesn't regard man.

5073.text: The land mourns and languishes. Lebanon is confounded and withers away. Sharon is like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel are stripped bare.

5074.text: "Now I will arise," says the Lord; "Now I will lift myself up. Now I will be exalted.

5075.text: You will conceive chaff. You will bring forth stubble. Your breath is a fire that will devour you.

5076.text: The peoples will be like the burning of lime, like thorns that are cut down and burned in the fire.

5077.text: Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and, you who are near, acknowledge my might."

5078.text: The sinners in Zion are afraid. Trembling has seized the godless ones. Who among us can live with the devouring fire? Who among us can live with everlasting burning?

5079.text: He who walks righteously, and speaks blamelessly; He who despises the gain of oppressions, who gestures with his hands, refusing to take a bribe, who stops his ears from hearing of blood, and shuts his eyes from looking at evil-

5080.text: he will dwell on high. His place of defense will be the fortress of rocks. His bread will be supplied. His waters will be sure.

5081.text: Your eyes will see the king in his beauty. They will see a distant land.

5082.text: Your heart will meditate on the terror. Where is he who counted? Where is he who weighed? Where is he who counted the towers?

5083.text: You will no longer see the fierce people, a people of a deep speech that you can't comprehend, with a strange language that you can't understand.

5084.text: Look at Zion, the city of our appointed festivals. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a quiet habitation, a tent that won't be removed. Its stakes will never be plucked up, nor will any of its cords be broken.

5085.text: But there the Lord will be with us in majesty, a place of broad rivers and streams, in which no galley with oars will go, neither will any gallant ship pass by there.

5086.text: For the Lord is our judge. The Lord is our lawgiver. The Lord is our king. He will save us.

5087.text: Your rigging is untied. They couldn't strengthen the foot of their mast. They couldn't spread the sail. Then the prey of a great spoil was divided. The lame took the prey.

5088.text: The inhabitant won't say, "I am sick." The people who dwell therein will be forgiven their iniquity.

5089.text: Come near, you nations, to hear! Listen, you peoples. Let the earth and all it contains hear; the world, and everything that comes from it.

5090.text: For the Lord is enraged against all the nations, and angry with all their armies. He has utterly destroyed them. He has given them over for slaughter.

5091.text: Their slain will also be cast out, and the stench of their dead bodies will come up; and the mountains will melt in their blood.

5092.text: All of the army of the sky will be dissolved. The sky will be rolled up like a scroll, and all its armies will fade away, as a leaf fades from off a vine or a fig tree.

5093.text: For my sword has drunk its fill in the sky. Behold, it will come down on Edom, and on the people of my curse, for judgment.

5094.text: The Lord's sword is filled with blood. It is covered with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams; for the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah, And a great slaughter in the land of Edom.

5095.text: The wild oxen will come down with them, and the young bulls with the mighty bulls; and their land will be drunken with blood, and their dust made greasy with fat.

5096.text: For the Lord has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.

5097.text: Its streams will be turned into pitch, its dust into sulfur, And its land will become burning pitch.

5098.text: It won't be quenched night nor day. Its smoke will go up forever. From generation to generation, it will lie waste. No one will pass through it forever and ever.

5099.text: But the pelican and the porcupine will possess it. The owl and the raven will dwell in it. He will stretch the line of confusion over it, and the plumb line of emptiness.

5100.text: They shall call its nobles to the kingdom, but none shall be there; and all its princes shall be nothing.

5101.text: Thorns will come up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in its fortresses; and it will be a habitation of jackals, a court for ostriches.

5102.text: The wild animals of the desert will meet with the wolves, and the wild goat will cry to his fellow. Yes, the night creature shall settle there, and shall find herself a place of rest.

5103.text: The arrow snake will make her nest there, and lay, hatch, and gather under her shade. Yes, the kites will be gathered there, every one with her mate.

5104.text: Search in the book of the Lord, and read: not one of these will be missing. None will lack her mate. For my mouth has commanded, and his Spirit has gathered them.

5105.text: He has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided it to them with a measuring line. They shall possess it forever. From generation to generation they will dwell in it.

5106.text: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad. The desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose.

5107.text: It will blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing. Lebanon's glory Lebanon will be given to it, the excellence of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the Lord's glory, the excellence of our God.

5108.text: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.

5109.text: Tell those who have a fearful heart, "Be strong. Do not be afraid. Behold, your God will come with vengeance, God's retribution. He will come and save you.

5110.text: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped.

5111.text: Then the lame man will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will sing; for waters will break out in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.

5112.text: The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water. Grass with reeds and rushes will be in the habitation of jackals, where they lay.

5113.text: A highway will be there, a road, and it will be called The Holy Way. The unclean shall not pass over it, but it will be for those who walk in the Way. Wicked fools will not go there.

5114.text: No lion will be there, nor will any ravenous animal go up on it. They will not be found there; but the redeemed will walk there.

5115.text: The Lord's ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away."

5116.text: Now it happened in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all of the fortified cities of Judah, and captured them.

5117.text: The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to king Hezekiah with a large army. He stood by the aqueduct from the upper pool in the fuller's field highway.

5118.text: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder came out to him.

5119.text: Rabshakeh said to them, "Now tell Hezekiah, 'Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria, "What confidence is this in which you trust?

5120.text: I say that your counsel and strength for the war are only vain words. Now in whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me?

5121.text: Behold, you trust in the staff of this bruised reed, even in Egypt, which if a man leans on it, it will go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

5122.text: But if you tell me, 'We trust in the Lord our God,' isn't that he whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has taken away, and has said to Judah and to Jerusalem, 'You shall worship before this altar?'"

5123.text: Now therefore, please make a pledge to my master the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to set riders on them.

5124.text: How then can you turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master's servants, and put your trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?

5125.text: Have I come up now without the Lord against this land to destroy it? The Lord said to me, "Go up against this land, and destroy it."'"

5126.text: Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it; and do not speak to us in the Jews' language in the hearing of the people who are on the wall."

5127.text: But Rabshakeh said, "Has my master sent me only to your master and to you, to speak these words, and not to the men who sit on the wall, who will eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?"

5128.text: Then Rabshakeh stood, and called out with a loud voice in the Jews' language, and said, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!

5129.text: Thus says the king, 'Do not let Hezekiah deceive you; for he will not be able to deliver you.

5130.text: Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord, saying, "The Lord will surely deliver us. This city won't be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."'

5131.text: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria, 'Make your peace with me, and come out to me; and each of you eat from his vine, and each one from his fig tree, and each one of you drink the waters of his own cistern;

5132.text: until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.

5133.text: Beware lest Hezekiah persuade you, saying, "The Lord will deliver us." Have any of the gods of the nations delivered their lands from the hand of the king of Assyria?

5134.text: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?

5135.text: Who are they among all the gods of these countries that have delivered their country out of my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?'"

5136.text: But they remained silent, and said nothing in reply, for the king's commandment was, "Do not answer him."

5137.text: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and told him the words of Rabshakeh.

5138.text: It happened, when king Hezekiah heard it, that he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the Lord's house.

5139.text: He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.

5140.text: They said to him, "Thus says Hezekiah, 'This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of rejection; for the children have come to the birth, and there is no strength to bring forth.

5141.text: It may be the Lord your God will hear the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words which the Lord your God has heard. Therefore lift up your prayer for the remnant that is left.'"

5142.text: So the servants of king Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

5143.text: Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master, 'Thus says the Lord, "Do not be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.

5144.text: Behold, I will put a spirit in him and he will hear news, and will return to his own land. I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land."'"

5145.text: So Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah, for he had heard that he was departed from Lachish.

5146.text: He heard news concerning Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, "He has come out to fight against you." When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,

5147.text: "Thus you shall speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, 'Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you, saying, "Jerusalem won't be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."

5148.text: Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, by destroying them utterly. Shall you be delivered?

5149.text: Have the gods of the nations delivered them, which my fathers have destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the children of Eden who were in Telassar?

5150.text: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?'"

5151.text: Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then Hezekiah went up to the Lord's house, and spread it before the Lord.

5152.text: Hezekiah prayed to the Lord, saying,

5153.text: "Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, who is enthroned among the cherubim, you are the God, even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth.

5154.text: Turn your ear, Lord, and hear. Open your eyes, Lord, and behold. Hear all of the words of Sennacherib, who has sent to defy the living God.

5155.text: Truly, Lord, the kings of Assyria have destroyed all the countries and their land,

5156.text: and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were no gods, but the work of men's hands, wood and stone; therefore they have destroyed them.

5157.text: Now therefore, Lord our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are the Lord, even you only."

5158.text: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, 'Because you have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria,

5159.text: this is the word which the Lord has spoken concerning him. The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and ridiculed you. The daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.

5160.text: Whom have you defied and blasphemed? Against whom have you exalted your voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel.

5161.text: By your servants, have you defied the Lord, and have said, "With the multitude of my chariots I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the innermost parts of Lebanon. I will cut down its tall cedars and its choice fir trees. I will enter into its farthest height, the forest of its fruitful field.

5162.text: I have dug and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet I will dry up all the rivers of Egypt."

5163.text: Have you not heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it in ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to destroy fortified cities, turning them into ruinous heaps.

5164.text: Therefore their inhabitants had little power. They were dismayed and confounded. They were like the grass of the field, and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like a field before its crop has grown.

5165.text: But I know your sitting down, your going out, your coming in, and your raging against me.

5166.text: Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, therefore will I put my hook in your nose and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.

5167.text: This shall be the sign to you. You will eat this year that which grows of itself, and in the second year that which springs from the same; and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.

5168.text: The remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah will again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.

5169.text: For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go forth, and survivors will escape from Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.'

5170.text: Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the king of Assyria, 'He will not come to this city, nor shoot an arrow there, neither will he come before it with shield, nor cast up a mound against it.

5171.text: By the way that he came, by the same he shall return, and he shall not come to this city,' says the Lord.

5172.text: 'For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake, and for my servant David's sake.'"

5173.text: The angel of the Lord went out and struck one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the camp of the Assyrians. When men arose early in the morning, behold, these were all dead bodies.

5174.text: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, went away, returned to Nineveh, and stayed there.

5175.text: It happened, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Ararat. Esar Haddon his son reigned in his place.

5176.text: In those days was Hezekiah sick and near death. Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him, and said to him, "Thus says the Lord, 'Set your house in order, for you will die, and not live.'"

5177.text: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord,

5178.text: and said, "Remember now, the Lord, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in your sight." Hezekiah wept bitterly.

5179.text: Then the word of the Lord came to Isaiah, saying,

5180.text: "Go, and tell Hezekiah, 'Thus says the Lord, the God of David your father, "I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.

5181.text: I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.

5182.text: This shall be the sign to you from the Lord, that the Lord will do this thing that he has spoken.

5183.text: Behold, I will cause the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down on the sundial of Ahaz with the sun, to return backward ten steps. So the sun returned ten steps on the sundial on which it had gone down."'"

5184.text: The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and had recovered of his sickness.

5185.text: I said, "In the middle of my life I go into the gates of Sheol. I am deprived of the residue of my years."

5186.text: I said, "I won't see Yah, Yah in the land of the living. I will see man no more with the inhabitants of the world.

5187.text: My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me like a shepherd's tent. I have rolled up, like a weaver, my life. He will cut me off from the loom. From day even to night you will make an end of me.

5188.text: I waited patiently until morning. He breaks all my bones like a lion. From day even to night you will make an end of me.

5189.text: I chattered like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes weaken looking upward. Lord, I am oppressed. Be my security."

5190.text: What will I say? He has both spoken to me, and himself has done it. I will walk carefully all my years because of the anguish of my soul.

5191.text: Lord, men live by these things; and my spirit finds life in all of them: you restore me, and cause me to live.

5192.text: Behold, for peace I had great anguish, but you have in love for my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption; for you have cast all my sins behind your back.

5193.text: For Sheol can't praise you. Death can't celebrate you. Those who go down into the pit can't hope for your truth.

5194.text: The living, the living, he shall praise you, as I do this day. The father shall make known your truth to the children.

5195.text: The Lord will save me. Therefore we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our life in the house of the Lord.

5196.text: Now Isaiah had said, "Let them take a cake of figs, and lay it for a poultice on the boil, and he shall recover."

5197.text: Hezekiah also had said, "What is the sign that I will go up to the house of the Lord?"

5198.text: At that time, Merodach Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah; for he heard that he had been sick, and had recovered.

5199.text: Hezekiah was pleased with them, and showed them the house of his precious things, the silver, and the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, and all the house of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures. There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah did not show them.

5200.text: Then Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah, and asked him, "What did these men say? Where did they come from to you?" Hezekiah said, "They have come from a country far from me, even from Babylon."

5201.text: Then he asked, "What have they seen in your house?" Hezekiah answered, "They have seen all that is in my house. There is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them."

5202.text: Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the Lord of hosts:

5203.text: 'Behold, the days are coming when all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have stored up until this day, will be carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left,' says the Lord.

5204.text: 'They will take away your sons who will issue from you, whom you shall father, and they will be eunuchs in the king of Babylon's palace.'"

5205.text: Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The Lord's word which you have spoken is good." He said moreover, "For there will be peace and truth in my days."

5206.text: "Comfort, comfort my people," says your God.

5207.text: "Speak tenderly to Jerusalem; and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of the Lord's hand double for all her sins."

5208.text: The voice of one who calls out, "Prepare the way of the Lord in the wilderness! Make a level highway in the desert for our God.

5209.text: Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low. The uneven shall be made level, and the rough places a plain.

5210.text: The glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken it."

5211.text: The voice of one saying, "Cry!" One said, "What shall I cry?" "All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field.

5212.text: The grass withers, the flower fades, because the Lord's breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass.

5213.text: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever."

5214.text: You who tell good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. You who tell good news to Jerusalem, lift up your voice with strength. Lift it up. Do not be afraid. Say to the cities of Judah, "Behold, your God!"

5215.text: Behold, the Lord God will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.

5216.text: He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.

5217.text: Who has measured the waters of the sea in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the sky with his span, and calculated the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?

5218.text: Who has known the mind of the Lord, or has taught him as his counselor?

5219.text: Who did he take counsel with, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?

5220.text: Behold, the nations are like a drop in a bucket, and are regarded as a speck of dust on a balance. Behold, he lifts up the islands like a very little thing.

5221.text: Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor its animals sufficient for a burnt offering.

5222.text: All the nations are like nothing before him. They are regarded by him as less than nothing, and vanity.

5223.text: To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare to him?

5224.text: A workman has cast an image, and the goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts silver chains for it.

5225.text: He who is too impoverished for such an offering chooses a tree that will not rot. He seeks a skillful workman to set up an engraved image for him that will not be moved.

5226.text: Haven't you known? Haven't you heard, yet? Haven't you been told from the beginning? Haven't you understood from the foundations of the earth?

5227.text: It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in;

5228.text: who brings princes to nothing; who makes the judges of the earth like meaningless.

5229.text: They are planted scarcely. They are sown scarcely. Their stock has scarcely taken root in the ground. He merely blows on them, and they wither, and the whirlwind takes them away as stubble.

5230.text: "To whom then will you liken me? Who is my equal?" says the Holy One.

5231.text: Lift up your eyes on high, and see who has created these, who brings out their host by number. He calls them all by name; by the greatness of his might, and because he is strong in power, Not one is lacking.

5232.text: Why do you say, Jacob, and speak, Israel, "My way is hidden from the Lord, and the justice due me is disregarded by my God?"

5233.text: Haven't you known? Haven't you heard? The everlasting God, the Lord, The Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn't faint. He isn't weary. His understanding is unsearchable.

5234.text: He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.

5235.text: Even the youths faint and get weary, and the young men utterly fall;

5236.text: But those who wait for the Lord will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.

5237.text: "Keep silent before me, islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come near, then let them speak. Let's meet together for judgment.

5238.text: Who has raised up one from the east? Whom he called to his foot in righteousness? He hands over nations to him, and makes him rule over kings. He gives them like the dust to his sword, like the driven stubble to his bow.

5239.text: He pursues them, and passes by safely, Even by a way that he had not gone with his feet.

5240.text: Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, the Lord, the first, and with the last, I am he."

5241.text: The islands have seen, and fear. The ends of the earth tremble. They approach, and come.

5242.text: Everyone helps his neighbor. They say to their brothers, "Be strong!"

5243.text: So the carpenter encourages the goldsmith. He who smoothes with the hammer encourages him who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, "It is good;" and he fastens it with nails, that it might not totter.

5244.text: "But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend,

5245.text: You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, 'You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you away;'

5246.text: Do not be afraid, for I am with you. Do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.

5247.text: Behold, all those who are incensed against you will be disappointed and confounded. Those who strive with you will be like nothing, and shall perish.

5248.text: You will seek them, and won't find them, even those who contend with you. Those who war against you will be as nothing, as a non-existent thing.
