7100.text: Her adversaries have become the head, her enemies prosper; for the Lord has afflicted her for the multitude of her transgressions: her young children have gone into captivity before the adversary.

7101.text: All majesty has departed from the daughter of Zion: her leaders have become like deer that find no pasture, they fled exhausted before the pursuer.

7102.text: Jerusalem remembers in the days of her affliction and wandering all her precious things that were from the days of old: when her people fell into the hand of the adversary, and no one helped her. The adversaries saw her, they mocked at her desolations.

7103.text: Jerusalem has grievously sinned; therefore she has become as an unclean thing; all who honored her despise her, because they have seen her nakedness: yes, she groans, and turns away.

7104.text: Her filthiness was in her skirts; she did not remember her latter end; therefore her fall was astonishing; she has no comforter. "Look, Lord, on my affliction, for the enemy has magnified himself."

7105.text: The adversary has spread out his hand on all her precious things: for she has seen that the nations have entered into her sanctuary, concerning whom you commanded that they should not enter into your assembly.

7106.text: All her people sigh, they seek bread; they have given their precious things for food to refresh the soul. "Look, Lord, and see, for I am despised."

7107.text: Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look, and see if there is any sorrow like my sorrow, which is brought on me, with which the Lord has afflicted me in the day of his fierce anger.

7108.text: From on high he has sent fire into my bones, and it overcame them. He has spread a net for my feet, he has turned me back. He has made me desolate and faint all the day.

7109.text: My transgressions are bound into a yoke; by his hand they are fastened together, they are set upon my neck; he has made my strength to fail. The Lord has delivered me into their hands, against whom I am not able to stand.

7110.text: The Lord has rejected all my mighty men in my midst; he has called a solemn assembly against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden as in a winepress the virgin daughter of Judah.

7111.text: For these things I weep; my eyes, my eyes flow with tears; because the comforter who should refresh my soul is far from me. My children are desolate, because the enemy has prevailed.

7112.text: Zion spreads forth her hands; there is none to comfort her. The Lord has commanded concerning Jacob, that those who are around him should be his adversaries. Jerusalem is among them as an unclean thing.

7113.text: The Lord is righteous, for I have rebelled against his commandment. Please listen all you people, and see my suffering. My virgins and my young men have gone into captivity.

7114.text: I called for my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city, while they searched for food to refresh their souls.

7115.text: See, Lord, for I am in distress; my stomach churns; my heart is turned within me; for I have grievously rebelled. Outside the sword bereaves, inside there is death.

7116.text: They have heard that I groan; there is none to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble; they are glad that you have done it. Bring the day that you have proclaimed, so that they shall end up like me.

7117.text: Let all their wickedness come before you. Do to them, as you have done to me for all my transgressions. For my groans are many, and my heart is faint.

7118.text: ALEPH How the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger! He has cast down from heaven to the earth the splendor of Israel, and hasn't remembered his footstool in the day of his anger.

7119.text: The Lord has swallowed up all the habitations of Jacob, and has not pitied. He has thrown down in his wrath the strongholds of the daughter of Judah. He has brought them down to the ground; he has humiliated the kingdom and its princes.

7120.text: He has cut off in fierce anger all the strength of Israel. He has drawn back his right hand before the enemy. He has blazed in Jacob like a flaming fire, which devours all around.

7121.text: He has bent his bow like an enemy; his right hand he has positioned like an adversary. He killed all that were pleasant to the eye. In the tent of the daughter of Zion he has poured out his wrath like fire.

7122.text: The Lord has become as an enemy; he has swallowed up Israel; he has swallowed up all her palaces and has destroyed its strongholds. He has multiplied in the daughter of Judah mourning and lamentation.

7123.text: He has done violence to his temple, as if it were a garden; he has destroyed his place of assembly. The Lord has caused solemn assembly and Sabbath to be forgotten in Zion. He has spurned in his fierce anger the king and the priest.

7124.text: The Lord has rejected his altar, he has disowned his sanctuary, and has given up into the hand of the enemy the walls of her palaces. They have made a shout in the house of the Lord, as in the day of a solemn assembly.

7125.text: The Lord has determined to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion. He has stretched out the line, he has not withdrawn his hand from destroying. He has made the rampart and wall to lament; they languish together.

7126.text: Her gates are sunk into the ground; he has destroyed and broken her bars. Her king and her princes are among the nations where the law is no more, and her prophets find no vision from the Lord.

7127.text: The elders of the daughter of Zion sit on the ground in silence. They have cast up dust on their heads; they have clothed themselves with sackcloth. The virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

7128.text: My eyes are worn out from weeping, my stomach is churning. My heart is poured on the earth, because of the destruction of the daughter of my people, because the young children and the infants faint in the streets of the city.

7129.text: They tell their mothers, "Where is grain and wine?" When they faint as the wounded in the streets of the city, as their lives fade away in their mothers' bosom.

7130.text: What shall I testify of you? What shall I liken to you, daughter of Jerusalem? What shall I compare to you, that I may comfort you, virgin daughter of Zion? For your ruin is great like the sea. Who can heal you?

7131.text: Your prophets have seen for you false and deceptive visions. They have not uncovered your iniquity, to bring back your captivity, but have seen for you false and misleading oracles.

7132.text: All that pass by clap their hands at you, they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying, "Is this the city that men called 'The perfection of beauty,' 'The joy of the whole earth'?"

7133.text: All your enemies have opened wide their mouth against you. They hiss and gnash the teeth; they say, "We have swallowed her up. Certainly this is the day that we looked for; we have found, we have seen it."

7134.text: The Lord has done that which he purposed, he has fulfilled his word that he commanded in the days of old. He has thrown down, and has not pitied. He has caused the enemy to gloat over you and exalted the horn of your adversaries.

7135.text: Their heart cried to the Lord. O wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears run down like a river day and night. Give yourself no respite; do not let your tears cease.

7136.text: Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches. Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands toward him for the life of your young children, that faint for hunger at the head of every street.

7137.text: Look, Lord, and see to whom you have done like this! Shall the women eat their fruit, the children that are dandled in the hands? Shall the priest and the prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?

7138.text: The youth and the old man lie on the ground in the streets; my virgins and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have killed them in the day of your anger; you have slaughtered, without pity.

7139.text: You have called, as in the day of a solemn assembly, my terrors on every side. There was none that escaped or remained in the day of the Lord's anger. Those that I have borne and brought up has my enemy destroyed.

7140.text: ALEPH I am the man that has seen affliction by the rod of his wrath.

7141.text: He has led me and caused me to walk in darkness, and not in light.

7142.text: Surely against me he turns his hand again and again all the day.

7143.text: My flesh and my skin he has made old; he has broken my bones.

7144.text: He has built against me, and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.

7145.text: He has made me to dwell in dark places, like those that have been long dead.

7146.text: He has walled me in, so I can't escape; he has made my chains heavy.

7147.text: Yes, when I cry, and call for help, he shuts out my prayer.

7148.text: He has walled up my ways with cut stone; he has made my paths crooked.

7149.text: He is to me as a bear lying in wait, as a lion in hiding.

7150.text: He has obstructed my path, and torn me in pieces; he has made me desolate.

7151.text: He has bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.

7152.text: He has caused the arrows of his quiver to pierce my inward parts.

7153.text: I have become a laughingstock to all my people, and their song all the day.

7154.text: He has filled me with bitterness, he has given me in full measure wormwood.

7155.text: He has also broken my teeth with gravel; he has pressed me down in the dust.

7156.text: You have removed my soul far away from peace; I have forgotten what prosperity is.

7157.text: And I said, "My strength and my hope has perished from the Lord."

7158.text: Remember my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the gall.

7159.text: My soul considers them, and is depressed.

7160.text: But this I call to my mind; therefore I have hope:

7161.text: The Lord's faithful love does not cease; his compassion does not fail.

7162.text: They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.

7163.text: "The Lord is my portion," says my soul, "therefore will I hope in him."

7164.text: The Lord is good to those who wait for him, to the soul that seeks him.

7165.text: It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.

7166.text: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke while he is young.

7167.text: Let him sit alone and keep silence when he is disciplining him.

7168.text: Let him put his mouth to the dust, there may yet be hope.

7169.text: Let him give his cheek to him who strikes him; let him be filled with insults.

7170.text: For the Lord will not reject forever.

7171.text: For though he may cause grief, yet he will have compassion according to the abundance of his loving kindness.

7172.text: For he is not predisposed to bring affliction or suffering to the children of men.

7173.text: To crush under foot all the prisoners of the earth;

7174.text: to deprive a man of justice before the face of the Most High,

7175.text: to subvert a man in his cause, the Lord does not approve.

7176.text: Who can speak a thing and have it come to pass, unless the Lord has commanded it?

7177.text: Doesn't both calamity and good come out of the mouth of the Most High?

7178.text: Why does a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?

7179.text: Let us examine and search our ways, and return to the Lord.

7180.text: Let us lift up our heart with our hands to God in the heavens.

7181.text: We have transgressed and have rebelled, and you have not forgiven.

7182.text: You have covered yourself with anger and pursued us; you killed without sparing.

7183.text: You have covered yourself with a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through.

7184.text: You have made us rubbish and refuse in the midst of the peoples.

7185.text: All our enemies have opened their mouth wide against us.

7186.text: Fear and the pit have come on us, devastation and destruction.

7187.text: Streams of tears run down from my eyes because of the destruction of the daughter of my people.

7188.text: My tears flow and do not cease, without respite,

7189.text: until the Lord looks down and sees from heaven.

7190.text: My eyes bring my soul grief, because of all the daughters of my city.

7191.text: They have chased me relentlessly like a bird, those who are my enemies without cause.

7192.text: They have cut off my life in a pit, and have cast a stone on me.

7193.text: Waters flowed over my head; I said, 'I am finished.'

7194.text: I called on your name, Lord, out of the depths of the pit.

7195.text: You heard my voice; do not hide your ear at my sighs, to my cry.

7196.text: You drew near in the day that I called on you; you said, "Do not be afraid."

7197.text: Lord, you have taken up the case for my soul; you have redeemed my life.

7198.text: Lord, you have seen the wrong done to me; judge my case.

7199.text: You have seen all their vengeance and all their plots against me.

7200.text: You have heard their insults, Lord, and all their plots against me.

7201.text: The lips of those that rose up against me, and their plots against me all day long.

7202.text: Behold their sitting down, and their rising up; I am their mocking song.

7203.text: You will render to them what they deserve, Lord, according to the work of their hands.

7204.text: You will give them hardness of heart as your curse to them.

7205.text: You will pursue them in anger, and destroy them from under the heavens of the Lord.

7206.text: ALEPH How the gold has become dim! How the most pure gold has changed! The stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the head of every street.

7207.text: The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, How they are regarded as clay jars, the work of the hands of the potter!

7208.text: Even the jackals offer the breast, they nurse their young ones, but the daughter of my people has become cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.

7209.text: The nursing infant's tongue sticks to the roof of his mouth for thirst. The young children ask for bread, but no one gives to them.

7210.text: Those who ate delicacies are destitute in the streets. Those who were brought up in purple embrace ash heaps.

7211.text: For the iniquity of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in an instant, and no hands were laid on her.

7212.text: Her consecrated ones were purer than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies more ruddy than rubies, their appearance was like lapis lazuli.

7213.text: They appear darker than soot; they are not known in the streets. Their skin cleaves to their bones; it is withered and has become as dry as a stick.

7214.text: Those who are killed with the sword are better than those who are killed with hunger; those who waste away, pierced through, for lack of the fruits of the field.

7215.text: The hands of the compassionate women have cooked their own children; they were their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.

7216.text: The Lord has accomplished his wrath, he has poured out his fierce anger; he has kindled a fire in Zion, which has devoured its foundations.

7217.text: The kings of the earth did not believe, neither all the inhabitants of the world, that the adversary or the enemy would enter into the gates of Jerusalem.

7218.text: It is because of the sins of her prophets, and the iniquities of her priests, that have shed the blood of the just in the midst of her.

7219.text: They wander as blind men in the streets, they are polluted with blood, so that men can't touch their garments.

7220.text: "Turn away!" they cried to them, "Unclean! depart, depart, do not touch!" When they fled away and wandered, men said among the nations, "They shall not live here anymore."

7221.text: The Lord himself has scattered them; he will no more regard them. They did not respect the priests, they did not favor the elders.

7222.text: Our eyes still fail, looking in vain for our help. In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save.

7223.text: They hunt our steps, so that we can't go in our streets. Our end is near, our days are fulfilled; for our end has come.

7224.text: Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the sky. They chased us on the mountains, they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.

7225.text: The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the Lord, was taken in their pits; of whom we said, "Under his shadow we can live among the nations."

7226.text: Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom, that dwell in the land of Uz. The cup shall pass through to you also; you will get drunk, and shall make yourself naked.

7227.text: The punishment of your iniquity is accomplished, daughter of Zion; he will no more carry you away into captivity. He will visit your iniquity, daughter of Edom; he will uncover your sins.

7228.text: Remember, Lord, what has come on us. Look, and see our disgrace.

7229.text: Our inheritance is turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.

7230.text: We are orphans and fatherless. Our mothers are like widows.

7231.text: We have to pay for a drink of water; our wood is sold to us.

7232.text: Our pursuers are on our necks; we are weary, and have no rest.

7233.text: We have submitted to the Egyptians and to the Assyrians, to get enough bread.

7234.text: Our fathers sinned, and are no more; we have borne their iniquities.

7235.text: Servants rule over us: There is none to deliver us out of their hand.

7236.text: We get our bread at the peril of our lives, because of the sword in the wilderness.

7237.text: Our skin is hot like an oven, because of the burning heat of famine.

7238.text: They raped the women in Zion, the virgins in the cities of Judah.

7239.text: Princes were hanged by their hands; elders were shown no respect.

7240.text: The young men grind at the mill; the boys stagger under loads of wood.

7241.text: The elders have gone from the gate, the young men from their music.

7242.text: The joy of our heart has ceased; our dancing is turned into mourning.

7243.text: The crown is fallen from our head; woe to us, for we have sinned!

7244.text: For this our heart is faint; for these things our eyes grow dim.

7245.text: For the mountain of Zion, which is desolate; the foxes walk on it.

7246.text: You, Lord, abide forever; your throne is from generation to generation.

7247.text: Why do you keep on forgetting us? Why do you forsake us so long?

7248.text: Restore us to you, Lord, and we shall be restored; renew our days as in former times,

7249.text: unless you have completely rejected us and are angry with us beyond measure.

7250.text: Now it happened in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth of the month, as I was among the captives by the river Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.

7251.text: In the fifth of the month, which was the fifth year of king Jehoiachin's captivity,

7252.text: the word of the Lord came expressly to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was there on him.

7253.text: I looked, and behold, a stormy wind came out of the north, a great cloud, with flashing lightning, and a brightness around it, and out of its midst as it were glowing metal, out of the midst of the fire.

7254.text: Out of its midst came the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: they had the likeness of a man.

7255.text: Everyone had four faces, and each one of them had four wings.

7256.text: Their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot; and they sparkled like burnished brass.

7257.text: They had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and the four of them had their faces and their wings thus:

7258.text: their wings were joined one to another; they didn't turn when they went; each one went straight forward.

7259.text: As for the likeness of their faces, they had the face of a man; and the four of them had the face of a lion on the right side; and the four of them had the face of an ox on the left side; the four of them also had the face of an eagle.

7260.text: Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above. Two wings of each one touched another, and two covered their bodies.

7261.text: Each one went straight forward: where the spirit was to go, they went; they didn't turn when they went.

7262.text: As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches: the fire went up and down among the living creatures; and the fire was bright, and out of the fire went forth lightning.

7263.text: The living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning.

7264.text: Now as I saw the living creatures, behold, one wheel on the earth beside the living creatures, for each of the four faces of it.

7265.text: The appearance of the wheels and their work was like a beryl: and the four of them had one likeness; and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel within a wheel.

7266.text: When they went, they went in their four directions: they didn't turn when they went.

7267.text: As for their rims, they were high and dreadful; and the four of them had their rims full of eyes all around.

7268.text: When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them; and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.

7269.text: Wherever the spirit was to go, they went; there was the spirit to go: and the wheels were lifted up beside them; for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.

7270.text: When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up beside them: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.

7271.text: Over the head of the living creature there was the likeness of an expanse, like the awesome crystal to look on, stretched forth over their heads above.

7272.text: Under the expanse were their wings straight, the one toward the other: each one had two which covered on this side, and every one had two which covered on that side, their bodies.

7273.text: When they went, I heard the noise of their wings like the noise of great waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a noise of tumult like the noise of an army: when they stood, they let down their wings.

7274.text: There was a voice above the expanse that was over their heads: when they stood, they let down their wings.

7275.text: Above the expanse that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone; and on the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man on it above.

7276.text: I saw as it were glowing metal, as the appearance of fire within it all around, from the appearance of his waist and upward; and from the appearance of his waist and downward I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and there was brightness around him.

7277.text: As the appearance of the rainbow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke.

7278.text: He said to me, "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."

7279.text: The Spirit entered into me when he spoke to me, and set me on my feet; and I heard him who spoke to me.

7280.text: He said to me, "Son of man, I send you to the children of Israel, to a nation of rebels who have rebelled against me. They and their fathers have transgressed against me even to this very day.

7281.text: The children are impudent and stiff-hearted: I am sending you to them; and you shall tell them, 'Thus says the Lord God.'

7282.text: They, whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear, (for they are a rebellious house), yet shall know that there has been a prophet among them.

7283.text: You, son of man, do not be afraid of them, neither be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns are with you, and you do dwell among scorpions: do not be afraid of their words, nor be dismayed at their looks, though they are a rebellious house.

7284.text: You shall speak my words to them, whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear; for they are most rebellious.

7285.text: But you, son of man, hear what I tell you; do not be rebellious like that rebellious house: open your mouth, and eat that which I give you."

7286.text: When I looked, behold, a hand was put forth to me; and, behold, a scroll of a book was therein;

7287.text: He spread it before me: and it was written within and without; and there were written therein lamentations, and mourning, and woe.

7288.text: He said to me, "Son of man, eat that which you find. Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel."

7289.text: So I opened my mouth, and he caused me to eat the scroll.

7290.text: He said to me, "Son of man, cause your belly to eat, and fill your bowels with this scroll that I give you." Then I ate it; and it was as sweet as honey in my mouth.

7291.text: He said to me, "Son of man, go to the house of Israel, and speak my words to them.

7292.text: For you are not sent to a people of a strange speech and of a hard language, but to the house of Israel;

7293.text: not to many peoples of a strange speech and of a hard language, whose words you can not understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.

7294.text: But the house of Israel will not listen to you; for they will not listen to me: for all the house of Israel are obstinate and hard-hearted.

7295.text: Behold, I have made your face hard against their faces, and your forehead hard against their foreheads.

7296.text: As an adamant harder than flint have I made your forehead: do not be afraid of them, neither be dismayed at their looks, though they are a rebellious house."

7297.text: Moreover he said to me, "Son of man, all my words that I shall speak to you receive in your heart, and hear with your ears.

7298.text: Go to them of the captivity, to the children of your people, and speak to them, and tell them, 'Thus says the Lord God'; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.

7299.text: Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing, saying, "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place."

7300.text: I heard the noise of the wings of the living creatures as they touched one another, and the noise of the wheels beside them, even the noise of a great rushing.

7301.text: So the Spirit lifted me up, and took me away; and I went in bitterness, in the anger of my spirit; and the hand of the Lord was strong on me.

7302.text: Then I came to them of the exiles at Tel Aviv, that lived by the river Chebar, and to where they lived; and I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days.

7303.text: It happened at the end of seven days, that the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7304.text: "Son of man, I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel: therefore hear the word from my mouth, and give them warning from me.

7305.text: When I tell the wicked, 'You shall surely die'; and you give him no warning, nor speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at your hand.

7306.text: Yet if you warn the wicked, and he doesn't turn from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity; but you have delivered your soul.

7307.text: "Again, when a righteous man does turn from his righteousness, and commit iniquity, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he shall die: because you have not given him warning, he shall die in his sin, and his righteous deeds which he has done shall not be remembered; but his blood will I require at your hand.

7308.text: Nevertheless if you warn the righteous man, that the righteous not sin, and he does not sin, he shall surely live, because he took warning; and you have delivered your soul."

7309.text: The hand of the Lord was there on me; and he said to me, "Arise, go forth into the plain, and I will there talk with you."

7310.text: Then I arose, and went forth into the plain: and behold, the glory of the Lord stood there, as the glory which I saw by the river Chebar; and I fell on my face.

7311.text: Then the Spirit entered into me, and set me on my feet; and he spoke with me, and said to me, "Go, shut yourself inside your house.

7312.text: But you, son of man, behold, they shall lay bands on you, and shall bind you with them, and you shall not go out among them:

7313.text: and I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, that you shall be mute, and shall not be to them a reprover; for they are a rebellious house.

7314.text: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall tell them, 'Thus says the Lord God': He who hears, let him hear; and he who forbears, let him forbear: for they are a rebellious house.

7315.text: "You also, son of man, take a tile, and lay it before yourself, and portray on it a city, even Jerusalem:

7316.text: and lay siege against it, and build forts against it, and cast up a mound against it; set camps also against it, and plant battering rams against it all around.

7317.text: Take for yourself an iron pan, and set it for a wall of iron between you and the city: and set your face toward it, and it shall be besieged, and you shall lay siege against it. This shall be a sign to the house of Israel.

7318.text: "Moreover lie on your left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel on it; according to the number of the days that you shall lie on it, you shall bear their iniquity.

7319.text: For I have appointed the years of their iniquity to be to you a number of days, even three hundred ninety days: so you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.

7320.text: "Again, when you have accomplished these, you shall lie on your right side, and shall bear the iniquity of the house of Judah: forty days, each day for a year, have I appointed it to you.

7321.text: You shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm uncovered; and you shall prophesy against it.

7322.text: Behold, I lay bands on you, and you shall not turn you from one side to the other, until you have accomplished the days of your siege.

7323.text: "Take for yourself also wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentils, and millet, and spelt, and put them in one vessel, and make bread of it; according to the number of the days that you shall lie on your side, even three hundred ninety days, you shall eat of it.

7324.text: Your food which you shall eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day: from time to time you shall eat it.

7325.text: You shall drink water by measure, the sixth part of a hin: from time to time you shall drink.

7326.text: You shall eat it as barley cakes, and you shall bake it in their sight with dung that comes out of man."

7327.text: The Lord said, "Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their bread unclean, among the nations where I will drive them."

7328.text: Then I said, "Ah Lord God! Behold, my soul has not been polluted; for from my youth up even until now have I not eaten of that which dies of itself, or is torn of animals; neither came there abominable flesh into my mouth."

7329.text: Then he said to me, "Behold, I have given you cow's dung for man's dung, and you shall prepare your bread thereon."

7330.text: Moreover he said to me, "Son of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem: and they shall eat bread by weight, and with fearfulness; and they shall drink water by measure, and in dismay:

7331.text: that they may want bread and water, and be dismayed one with another, and pine away in their iniquity.

7332.text: "You, son of man, take a sharp sword; You shall take it as a barber's razor to you, and shall cause it to pass on your head and on your beard: then take balances to weigh, and divide the hair.

7333.text: A third part you shall burn in the fire in the midst of the city, when the days of the siege are fulfilled; and you shall take a third part, and strike with the sword around it; and a third part you shall scatter to the wind, and I will draw out a sword after them.

7334.text: You shall take of it a few in number, and bind them in your skirts.

7335.text: Of these again you shall take, and cast them into the midst of the fire, and burn them in the fire; from it shall a fire come forth into all the house of Israel."

7336.text: "Thus says the Lord God: 'This is Jerusalem; I have set her in the midst of the nations, and countries are around her.

7337.text: She has rebelled against my ordinances in doing wickedness more than the nations, and against my statutes more than the countries that are around her; for they have rejected my ordinances, and as for my statutes, they have not walked in them.'

7338.text: "Therefore thus says the Lord God: 'Because you are turbulent more than the nations that are around you, and have not walked in my statutes, neither have kept my ordinances, neither have done after the ordinances of the nations that are around you';

7339.text: therefore thus says the Lord God: 'Behold, I, even I, am against you; and I will execute judgments in the midst of you in the sight of the nations.

7340.text: I will do in you that which I have not done, and whereunto I will not do any more the like, because of all your abominations.

7341.text: Therefore the fathers shall eat the sons in the midst of you, and the sons shall eat their fathers; and I will execute judgments on you; and the whole remnant of you will I scatter to all the winds.'

7342.text: "'Therefore as I live,' says the Lord God, 'surely, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things, and with all your abominations, therefore will I also diminish you; neither shall my eye spare, and I also will have no pity.

7343.text: A third part of you shall die with the pestilence, and with famine shall they be consumed in the midst of you; and a third part shall fall by the sword around you; and a third part I will scatter to all the winds, and will draw out a sword after them.

7344.text: Thus shall my anger be accomplished, and I will cause my wrath toward them to rest, and I shall be comforted; and they shall know that I, the Lord, have spoken in my zeal, when I have accomplished my wrath on them.

7345.text: Moreover I will make you a desolation and a reproach among the nations that are around you, in the sight of all that pass by.

7346.text: So it shall be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment, to the nations that are around you, when I shall execute judgments on you in anger and in wrath, and in wrathful rebukes; (I, the Lord, have spoken it;)

7347.text: when I shall send on them the evil arrows of famine, that are for destruction, which I will send to destroy you: and I will increase the famine on you, and will break your staff of bread;

7348.text: and I will send on you famine and evil animals, and they shall bereave you; and pestilence and blood shall pass through you; and I will bring the sword on you: I, the Lord, have spoken it.'"

7349.text: The word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7350.text: "Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy to them,

7351.text: and say, 'You mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God: Thus says the Lord God to the mountains and to the hills, to the watercourses and to the valleys: "Behold, I, even I, will bring a sword on you, and I will destroy your high places.

7352.text: Your altars shall become desolate, and your incense altars shall be broken; and I will cast down your slain men before your idols.

7353.text: I will lay the dead bodies of the children of Israel before their idols; and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

7354.text: In all your dwelling places the cities shall be laid waste, and the high places shall be desolate; that your altars may be laid waste and made desolate, and your idols may be broken and cease, and your incense altars may be cut down, and your works may be abolished.

7355.text: The slain shall fall in the midst of you, and you shall know that I am the Lord.

7356.text: "'"Yet will I leave a remnant, in that you shall have some that escape the sword among the nations, when you shall be scattered through the countries.

7357.text: Those of you that escape shall remember me among the nations where they shall be carried captive, how that I have been broken with their lewd heart, which has departed from me, and with their eyes, which play the prostitute after their idols: and they shall loathe themselves in their own sight for the evils which they have committed in all their abominations.

7358.text: They shall know that I am the Lord: I have not said in vain that I would bring this disaster on them."'"

7359.text: "Thus says the Lord God: 'Strike with your hand, and stamp with your foot, and say, "Alas!" because of all the evil abominations of the house of Israel; for they shall fall by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence.

7360.text: He who is far off shall die of the pestilence; and he who is near shall fall by the sword; and he who remains and is besieged shall die by the famine: thus will I accomplish my wrath on them.

7361.text: You shall know that I am the Lord, when their slain men shall be among their idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the tops of the mountains, and under every green tree, and under every thick oak, the places where they offered pleasant aroma to all their idols.

7362.text: I will stretch out my hand on them, and make the land desolate and waste, from the wilderness toward Diblah, throughout all their habitations: and they shall know that I am the Lord."'"

7363.text: Moreover the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7364.text: "You, son of man, thus says the Lord God to the land of Israel, 'An end: the end has come on the four corners of the land.

7365.text: Now is the end on you, and I will send my anger on you, and will judge you according to your ways; and I will bring on you all your abominations.

7366.text: My eye shall not spare you, neither will I have pity; but I will bring your ways on you, and your abominations shall be in the midst of you: and you shall know that I am the Lord.'"

7367.text: "Thus says the Lord God: 'A disaster, a unique disaster; behold, it comes.

7368.text: An end has come, the end has come; it awakes against you; behold, it comes.

7369.text: Your doom has come to you, inhabitant of the land: the time has come, the day is near, a day of tumult, and not of joyful shouting, on the mountains.

7370.text: Now will I shortly pour out my wrath on you, and accomplish my anger against you, and will judge you according to your ways; and I will bring on you all your abominations.

7371.text: My eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: I will bring on you according to your ways; and your abominations shall be in the midst of you; and you shall know that I, the Lord, do strike.

7372.text: Behold, the day, behold, it comes: your doom is gone forth; the rod has blossomed, pride has budded.'

7373.text: "Violence has risen up into a rod of wickedness. None of them shall remain, nor of their multitude, nor of their wealth. There shall be nothing of value among them.

7374.text: The time has come, the day draws near: do not let the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn; for wrath is on all its multitude.

7375.text: For the seller shall not return to that which is sold, although they be yet alive: for the vision is touching the whole multitude of it, none shall return; neither shall any strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life.

7376.text: They have blown the trumpet, and have made all ready; but none goes to the battle; for my wrath is on all its multitude.

7377.text: The sword is outside, and the pestilence and the famine within: he who is in the field shall die with the sword: and he who is in the city, famine and pestilence shall devour him.

7378.text: But those of those who escape shall escape, and shall be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, every one in his iniquity.

7379.text: All hands shall be feeble, and all knees shall be weak as water.

7380.text: They shall also clothe themselves with sackcloth, and horror shall cover them; and shame shall be on all faces, and baldness on all their heads.

7381.text: They shall cast their silver in the streets, and their gold shall be as an unclean thing; their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord: they shall not satisfy their souls, neither fill their bowels; because it has been the stumbling block of their iniquity.

7382.text: As for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty; but they made the images of their abominations and their detestable things therein: therefore have I made it to them as an unclean thing.

7383.text: I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil; and they shall profane it.

7384.text: My face will I turn also from them, and they shall profane my secret place; and robbers shall enter into it, and profane it.

7385.text: "Make the chain; for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.

7386.text: Therefore I will bring the worst of the nations, and they shall possess their houses: I will also make the pride of the strong to cease; and their holy places shall be profaned.

7387.text: Destruction comes; and they shall seek peace, and there shall be none.

7388.text: Disaster shall come upon disaster, and rumor shall follow rumor; and they shall seek a vision from a prophet; but the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.

7389.text: The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation, and the hands of the people of the land shall be troubled: I will do to them after their way, and according to their own judgments will I judge them; and they shall know that I am the Lord."

7390.text: It happened in the sixth year, in the sixth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I sat in my house, and the elders of Judah sat before me, that the hand of the Lord God fell there on me.

7391.text: Then I saw, and behold, a likeness as the appearance of fire; from the appearance of his waist and downward, fire; and from his waist and upward, as the appearance of brightness, as it were glowing metal.

7392.text: He put forth the form of a hand, and took me by a lock of my head; and the Spirit lifted me up between earth and the sky, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the gate of the inner court that looks toward the north; where there was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes to jealousy.

7393.text: Behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, according to the appearance that I saw in the plain.

7394.text: Then he said to me, "Son of man, lift up your eyes now the way toward the north." So I lifted up my eyes the way toward the north, and see, northward of the gate of the altar this image of jealousy in the entry.

7395.text: He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what they do? Even the great abominations that the house of Israel do commit here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? But you shall again see yet other great abominations."

7396.text: He brought me to the door of the court; and when I looked, behold, a hole in the wall.

7397.text: Then he said to me, "Son of man, dig now in the wall": and when I had dug in the wall, behold, a door.

7398.text: He said to me, "Go in, and see the wicked abominations that they do here."

7399.text: So I went in and saw; and see, every form of creeping things, and abominable animals, and all the idols of the house of Israel, portrayed around on the wall.

7400.text: There stood before them seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel; and in their midst stood Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan, every man with his censer in his hand; and the odor of the cloud of incense went up.

7401.text: Then he said to me, "Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in his rooms of imagery? For they say, 'The Lord doesn't see us. The Lord has forsaken the land.'"

7402.text: He said also to me, "You shall again see yet other great abominations which they do."

7403.text: Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord's house which was toward the north; and see, there sat the women weeping for Tammuz.

7404.text: Then he said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? You shall again see yet greater abominations than these."

7405.text: He brought me into the inner court of the Lord's house; and see, at the door of the Lord's temple, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men, with their backs toward the Lord's temple, and their faces toward the east; and they were worshipping the sun toward the east.

7406.text: Then he said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations which they commit here? For they have filled the land with violence, and have turned again to provoke me to anger: and behold, they put the branch to their nose.

7407.text: Therefore will I also deal in wrath; my eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity; and though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, yet will I not hear them."

7408.text: Then he cried in my ears with a loud voice, saying, "Cause those who are in charge of the city to draw near, every man with his destroying weapon in his hand."

7409.text: Behold, six men came from the way of the upper gate, which lies toward the north, every man with his slaughter weapon in his hand; and one man in their midst clothed in linen, with a writer's inkhorn by his side. They went in, and stood beside the bronze altar.

7410.text: The glory of the God of Israel was gone up from the cherub, whereupon it was, to the threshold of the house: and he called to the man clothed in linen, who had the writer's inkhorn by his side.

7411.text: The Lord said to him, "Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark on the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry over all the abominations that are done in its midst."

7412.text: To the others he said in my hearing, "Go through the city after him, and strike: do not let your eye spare, neither have pity;

7413.text: kill utterly the old man, the young man and the virgin, and little children and women; but do not come near any man on whom is the mark: and begin at my sanctuary." Then they began at the old men that were before the house.

7414.text: He said to them, "Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain. Go forth!" They went forth, and struck in the city.

7415.text: It happened, while they were smiting, and I was left, that I fell on my face, and cried, and said, "Ah Lord God! Will you destroy all the residue of Israel in your pouring out of your wrath on Jerusalem?"

7416.text: Then he said to me, "The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great, and the land is full of blood, and the city full of perversion: for they say, 'The Lord has forsaken the land, and the Lord doesn't see.'

7417.text: As for me also, my eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity, but I will bring their way on their head."

7418.text: Behold, the man clothed in linen, who had the inkhorn by his side, reported the matter, saying, "I have done as you have commanded me."

7419.text: Then I looked, and saw, in the expanse that was over the head of the cherubim there appeared above them as it were a sapphire stone, as the appearance of the likeness of a throne.

7420.text: He spoke to the man clothed in linen, and said, "Go in between the whirling wheels, even under the cherub, and fill both your hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city." He went in as I watched.

7421.text: Now the cherubim stood on the right side of the house, when the man went in; and the cloud filled the inner court.

7422.text: The glory of the Lord mounted up from the cherub, and stood over the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of the Lord's glory.

7423.text: The sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard even to the outer court, as the voice of God Almighty when he speaks.

7424.text: It came to pass, when he commanded the man clothed in linen, saying, "Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim," that he went in, and stood beside a wheel.

7425.text: The cherub stretched forth his hand from between the cherubim to the fire that was between the cherubim, and took of it, and put it into the hands of him who was clothed in linen, who took it and went out.

7426.text: There appeared in the cherubim the form of a man's hand under their wings.

7427.text: I looked, and behold, four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside one cherub, and another wheel beside another cherub; and the appearance of the wheels was like a beryl stone.

7428.text: As for their appearance, the four of them had one likeness, like a wheel within a wheel.

7429.text: When they went, they went in their four directions: they didn't turn as they went, but to the place where the head looked they followed it; they didn't turn as they went.

7430.text: Their whole body, and their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes all around, even the wheels that the four of them had.

7431.text: As for the wheels, they were called in my hearing, "the whirling wheels."

7432.text: Every one had four faces: the first face was the face of the cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third face the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.

7433.text: The cherubim mounted up: this is the living creature that I saw by the river Chebar.

7434.text: When the cherubim went, the wheels went beside them; and when the cherubim lifted up their wings to mount up from the earth, the wheels also didn't turn from beside them.

7435.text: When they stood, these stood; and when they mounted up, these mounted up with them: for the spirit of the living creature was in them.

7436.text: The glory of the Lord went forth from over the threshold of the house, and stood over the cherubim.

7437.text: The cherubim lifted up their wings, and mounted up from the earth in my sight when they went forth, and the wheels beside them: and they stood at the door of the east gate of the Lord's house; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above.

7438.text: These were the living creatures that I saw under the God of Israel by the river Chebar; and I knew that they were cherubim.

7439.text: Every one had four faces, and every one four wings; and the likeness of the hands of a man was under their wings.

7440.text: As for the likeness of their faces, they were the faces which I saw by the river Chebar, their appearances and themselves; they went every one straight forward.

7441.text: Moreover the Spirit lifted me up, and brought me to the east gate of the Lord's house, which looks eastward: and see, at the door of the gate twenty-five men; and I saw in their midst Jaazaniah the son of Azzur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people.

7442.text: He said to me, "Son of man, these are the men who devise iniquity, and who give wicked counsel in this city;

7443.text: who say, 'The time is not near to build houses: this is the caldron, and we are the meat.'

7444.text: Therefore prophesy against them, prophesy, son of man."

7445.text: The Spirit of the Lord fell on me, and he said to me, "Speak, Thus says the Lord: 'Thus you have said, house of Israel; for I know the things that come into your mind.

7446.text: You have multiplied your slain in this city, and you have filled its streets with the slain.'

7447.text: Therefore thus says the Lord God: 'Your slain whom you have laid in its midst, they are the meat, and this is the caldron; but you shall be brought out of its midst.

7448.text: You have feared the sword; and I will bring the sword on you,' says the Lord God.

7449.text: 'I will bring you forth out of its midst, and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute judgments among you.

7450.text: You shall fall by the sword; I will judge you in the border of Israel; and you shall know that I am the Lord.

7451.text: This shall not be your caldron, neither shall you be the meat in its midst; I will judge you in the border of Israel;

7452.text: and you shall know that I am the Lord: for you have not walked in my statutes, neither have you executed my ordinances, but have done after the ordinances of the nations that are around you.'"

7453.text: It happened, when I prophesied, that Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. Then fell I down on my face, and cried with a loud voice, and said, "Ah Lord God! Will you make a full end of the remnant of Israel?"

7454.text: The word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7455.text: "Son of man, your brothers, even your brothers, the men of your relatives, and all the house of Israel, all of them, to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, 'Go far away from the Lord. This land has been given to us for a possession.'

7456.text: Therefore say, 'Thus says the Lord God: "Whereas I have removed them far off among the nations, and whereas I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them a sanctuary for a little while in the countries where they have come."'

7457.text: Therefore say, 'Thus says the Lord God: "I will gather you from the peoples, and assemble you out of the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel."

7458.text: They shall come there, and they shall take away all the detestable things of it and all its abominations from there.

7459.text: I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them a heart of flesh;

7460.text: that they may walk in my statutes, and keep my ordinances, and do them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God.

7461.text: But as for them whose heart walks after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I will bring their way on their own heads,' says the Lord God."

7462.text: Then the cherubim lifted up their wings, and the wheels were beside them; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above.

7463.text: The glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city, and stood on the mountain which is on the east side of the city.

7464.text: The Spirit lifted me up, and brought me in the vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea, to them of the captivity. So the vision that I had seen went up from me.

7465.text: Then I spoke to them of the captivity all the things that the Lord had shown me.

7466.text: The word of the Lord also came to me, saying,

7467.text: "Son of man, you dwell in the midst of the rebellious house, who have eyes to see, and do not see, who have ears to hear, and do not hear; for they are a rebellious house.

7468.text: Therefore, you son of man, prepare your stuff for moving, and move by day in their sight; and you shall move from your place to another place in their sight: it may be they will consider, though they are a rebellious house.

7469.text: You shall bring forth your stuff by day in their sight, as stuff for moving; and you shall go forth yourself at even in their sight, as when men go forth into exile.

7470.text: Dig through the wall in their sight, and carry your stuff out that way.

7471.text: In their sight you shall bear it on your shoulder, and carry it forth in the dark; you shall cover your face, so that you do not see the land: for I have set you for a sign to the house of Israel."

7472.text: I did so as I was commanded: I brought forth my stuff by day, as stuff for removing, and in the even I dug through the wall with my hand; I brought it forth in the dark, and bore it on my shoulder in their sight.

7473.text: In the morning came the word of the Lord to me, saying,

7474.text: "Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said to you, 'What are you doing?'

7475.text: Say to them, 'Thus says the Lord God: This burden concerns the prince in Jerusalem, and all the house of Israel among whom they are.'

7476.text: Say, 'I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done to them; they shall go into exile, into captivity.'

7477.text: "The prince who is among them shall bear on his shoulder in the dark, and shall go forth: they shall dig through the wall to carry out thereby: he shall cover his face, because he shall not see the land with his eyes.

7478.text: My net also will I spread on him, and he shall be taken in my snare; and I will bring him to Babylon to the land of the Chaldeans; yet shall he not see it, though he shall die there.

7479.text: I will scatter toward every wind all who are around him to help him, and all his bands; and I will draw out the sword after them.

7480.text: They shall know that I am the Lord, when I shall disperse them among the nations, and scatter them through the countries.

7481.text: But I will leave a few men of them from the sword, from the famine, and from the pestilence; that they may declare all their abominations among the nations where they come; and they shall know that I am the Lord."

7482.text: Moreover the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7483.text: "Son of man, eat your bread with quaking, and drink your water with trembling and with fearfulness;

7484.text: and tell the people of the land, 'Thus says the Lord God concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the land of Israel: They shall eat their bread with fearfulness, and drink their water in dismay, that her land may be desolate, and all that is therein, because of the violence of all those who dwell therein.

7485.text: The cities that are inhabited shall be laid waste, and the land shall be a desolation; and you shall know that I am the Lord.'"

7486.text: The word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7487.text: "Son of man, what is this proverb that you have in the land of Israel, saying, 'The days are prolonged, and every vision fails?'

7488.text: Tell them therefore, 'Thus says the Lord God: I will make this proverb to cease, and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Israel'; but tell them, 'The days are at hand, and the fulfillment of every vision.

7489.text: For there shall be no more any false vision nor flattering divination within the house of Israel.

7490.text: For I am the Lord; I will speak, and the word that I shall speak shall be performed; it shall be no more deferred: for in your days, rebellious house, will I speak the word, and will perform it,' says the Lord God."

7491.text: Again the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7492.text: "Son of man, behold, they of the house of Israel say, 'The vision that he sees is for many day to come, and he prophesies of times that are far off.'

7493.text: Therefore tell them, 'Thus says the Lord God: None of my words shall be deferred any more, but the word which I shall speak shall be performed, says the Lord God.'"

7494.text: The word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7495.text: "Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who prophesy, and say to those who prophesy out of their own heart, 'Hear the word of the Lord:

7496.text: Thus says the Lord God, "Woe to the foolish prophets, who follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!

7497.text: Israel, your prophets have been like foxes in the waste places.

7498.text: You have not gone up into the gaps, neither built up the wall for the house of Israel, to stand in the battle in the day of the Lord."

7499.text: They have seen falsehood and lying divination, who say, "The Lord says"; but the Lord has not sent them: and they have made men to hope that the word would be confirmed.

7500.text: "Haven't you seen a false vision, and haven't you spoken a lying divination, in that you say, "The Lord says"; but I have not spoken?

7501.text: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have spoken falsehood, and seen lies, therefore, behold, I am against you, says the Lord God.

7502.text: My hand shall be against the prophets who see false visions, and who divine lies: they shall not be in the council of my people, neither shall they be written in the writing of the house of Israel, neither shall they enter into the land of Israel; and you shall know that I am the Lord God.

7503.text: Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, 'Peace'; and there is no peace; and when one builds up a wall, behold, they plaster it with whitewash:

7504.text: tell those who plaster it with whitewash, that it shall fall: there shall be an overflowing shower; and you, great hailstones, shall fall; and a stormy wind shall tear it.

7505.text: Behold, when the wall has fallen, shall it not be said to you, 'Where is the plaster with which you have plastered it?'

7506.text: "'"Therefore thus says the Lord God: I will even tear it with a stormy wind in my wrath; and there shall be an overflowing shower in my anger, and great hailstones in wrath to consume it.

7507.text: So will I break down the wall that you have plastered with whitewash, and bring it down to the ground, so that its foundation shall be uncovered; and it shall fall, and you shall be consumed in its midst: and you shall know that I am the Lord.

7508.text: Thus will I accomplish my wrath on the wall, and on those who have plastered it with whitewash; and I will tell you, 'The wall is no more, neither those who plastered it;

7509.text: to wit, the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem, and who see visions of peace for her, and there is no peace,'"' says the Lord God."

7510.text: "You, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people, who prophesy out of their own heart; and prophesy against them,

7511.text: and say, 'Thus says the Lord God: "Woe to the women who sew pillows on all elbows, and make kerchiefs for the head of persons of every stature to hunt souls! Will you hunt the souls of my people, and save souls alive for yourselves?

7512.text: You have profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, to kill the souls who should not die, and to save the souls alive who should not live, by your lying to my people who listen to lies."

7513.text: "'Therefore thus says the Lord God: "Behold, I am against your pillows, with which you there hunt the souls to make them fly, and I will tear them from your arms; and I will let the souls go, even the souls whom you hunt to make them fly.

7514.text: Your kerchiefs also will I tear, and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand to be hunted; and you shall know that I am the Lord.

7515.text: Because with lies you have grieved the heart of the righteous, whom I have not made sad; and strengthened the hands of the wicked, that he should not return from his wicked way, and be saved alive:

7516.text: Therefore you shall no more see false visions, nor practice divination. I will deliver my people out of your hand; and you shall know that I am the Lord."'"

7517.text: Then came certain of the elders of Israel to me, and sat before me.

7518.text: The word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7519.text: "Son of man, these men have taken their idols into their heart, and put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face: should I be inquired of at all by them?

7520.text: Therefore speak to them, and tell them, 'Thus says the Lord God: "Every man of the house of Israel who takes his idols into his heart, and puts the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to the prophet; I the Lord will answer him therein according to the multitude of his idols;

7521.text: that I may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from me through their idols."'

7522.text: "Therefore tell the house of Israel, 'Thus says the Lord God: "Return, and turn yourselves from your idols; and turn away your faces from all your abominations.

7523.text: For everyone of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who live in Israel, who separates himself from me, and takes his idols into his heart, and puts the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to the prophet to inquire for himself of me; I the Lord will answer him by myself:

7524.text: and I will set my face against that man, and will make him an astonishment, for a sign and a proverb, and I will cut him off from the midst of my people; and you shall know that I am the Lord.

7525.text: "'"If the prophet is deceived and speaks a word, I, the Lord, have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand on him, and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel.

7526.text: They shall bear their iniquity: the iniquity of the prophet shall be even as the iniquity of him who seeks him;

7527.text: that the house of Israel may go no more astray from me, neither defile themselves any more with all their transgressions; but that they may be my people, and I may be their God," says the Lord God.'"

7528.text: The word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7529.text: "Son of man, when a land sins against me by committing a trespass, and I stretch out my hand on it, and break the staff of its bread, and send famine on it, and cut off from it man and animal;

7530.text: though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness, says the Lord God."

7531.text: "If I cause evil animals to pass through the land, and they ravage it, and it be made desolate, so that no man may pass through because of the animals;

7532.text: though these three men were in it, as I live," says the Lord God, "they should deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only should be delivered, but the land should be desolate.

7533.text: "Or if I bring a sword on that land, and say, 'Sword, go through the land'; so that I cut off from it man and animal;

7534.text: though these three men were in it, as I live, says the Lord God, they should deliver neither sons nor daughters, but they only should be delivered themselves.

7535.text: "Or if I send a pestilence into that land, and pour out my wrath on it in blood, to cut off from it man and animal;

7536.text: though Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, as I live, says the Lord God, they should deliver neither son nor daughter; they should but deliver their own souls by their righteousness.

7537.text: "For thus says the Lord God: 'How much more when I send my four severe judgments on Jerusalem, the sword, and the famine, and the evil animals, and the pestilence, to cut off from it man and animal!

7538.text: Yet, behold, therein shall be left a remnant that shall be carried forth, both sons and daughters: behold, they shall come forth to you, and you shall see their way and their doings; and you shall be comforted concerning the evil that I have brought on Jerusalem, even concerning all that I have brought on it.

7539.text: They shall comfort you, when you see their way and their doings; and you shall know that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it,' says the Lord God."

7540.text: The word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7541.text: "Son of man, what is the vine tree more than any tree, the vine-branch which is among the trees of the forest?

7542.text: Shall wood be taken of it to make any work? Or will men take a pin of it to hang any vessel thereon?

7543.text: Behold, it is cast into the fire for fuel; the fire has devoured both its ends, and its midst is burned: is it profitable for any work?

7544.text: Behold, when it was whole, it was meet for no work: how much less, when the fire has devoured it, and it is burned, shall it yet be meet for any work!

7545.text: "Therefore thus says the Lord God: 'As the vine tree among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so will I give the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

7546.text: I will set my face against them; they shall go forth from the fire, but the fire shall devour them; and you shall know that I am the Lord, when I set my face against them.

7547.text: I will make the land desolate, because they have committed a trespass,' says the Lord God."

7548.text: Again the word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7549.text: "Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations;

7550.text: and say, 'Thus says the Lord God to Jerusalem: Your birth and your birth is of the land of the Canaanite; the Amorite was your father, and your mother was a Hittite.

7551.text: As for your birth, in the day you were born your navel was not cut, neither were you washed in water to cleanse you; you weren't salted at all, nor swaddled at all.

7552.text: No eye pitied you, to do any of these things to you, to have compassion on you; but you were cast out in the open field, for that your person was abhorred, in the day that you were born.

7553.text: "'When I passed by you, and saw you wallowing in your blood, I said to you, Though you are in your blood, live; yes, I said to you, "Though you are in your blood, live."

7554.text: I caused you to multiply as that which grows in the field, and you increased and grew great, and you attained to excellent ornament; your breasts were fashioned, and your hair was grown; yet you were naked and bare.

7555.text: "'Now when I passed by you, and looked at you, behold, your time was the time of love; and I spread my skirt over you, and covered your nakedness: yes, I swore to you, and entered into a covenant with you,' says the Lord God, 'and you became mine.

7556.text: "'Then washed I you with water; yes, I thoroughly washed away your blood from you, and I anointed you with oil.

7557.text: I clothed you also with embroidered work, and shod you with sealskin, and I dressed you about with fine linen, and covered you with silk.

7558.text: I decked you with ornaments, and I put bracelets on your hands, and a chain on your neck.

7559.text: I put a ring on your nose, and earrings in your ears, and a beautiful crown on your head.

7560.text: Thus you were decked with gold and silver; and your clothing was of fine linen, and silk, and embroidered work; you ate fine flour, and honey, and oil; and you were exceeding beautiful, and you prospered to royal estate.

7561.text: Your renown went forth among the nations for your beauty; for it was perfect, through my majesty which I had put on you,' says the Lord God.

7562.text: "'But you trusted in your beauty, and played the prostitute because of your renown, and poured out your prostitution on everyone who passed by; his it was.

7563.text: You took of your garments, and made for yourselves high places decked with various colors, and played the prostitute on them: the like things shall not come, neither shall it be so.

7564.text: You also took your beautiful jewels of my gold and of my silver, which I had given you, and made for yourself images of men, and played the prostitute with them;

7565.text: and you took your embroidered garments, and covered them, and set my oil and my incense before them.

7566.text: My bread also which I gave you, fine flour, and oil, and honey, with which I fed you, you even set it before them for a pleasant aroma; and thus it was,' says the Lord God.

7567.text: "'Moreover you have taken your sons and your daughters, whom you have borne to me, and you have sacrificed these to them to be devoured. Was your prostitution a small matter,

7568.text: that you have slain my children, and delivered them up, in causing them to pass through the fire to them?

7569.text: In all your abominations and your prostitution you have not remembered the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, and were wallowing in your blood.

7570.text: "'It has happened after all your wickedness, ("Woe, woe to you!" says the Lord God),

7571.text: that you have built for yourselves a vaulted place, and have made yourselves a lofty place in every street.

7572.text: You have built your lofty place at the head of every way, and have made your beauty an abomination, and have opened your feet to everyone who passed by, and multiplied your prostitution.

7573.text: You have also committed sexual immorality with the Egyptians, your neighbors, great of flesh; and have multiplied your prostitution, to provoke me to anger.

7574.text: See therefore, I have stretched out my hand over you, and have diminished your ordinary food, and delivered you to the will of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who are ashamed of your lewd way.

7575.text: You have played the prostitute also with the Assyrians, because you were insatiable; yes, you have played the prostitute with them, and yet you weren't satisfied.

7576.text: You have moreover multiplied your prostitution to the land of merchants, to Chaldea; and yet you weren't satisfied with this.

7577.text: "'How weak is your heart, says the Lord God, since you do all these things, the work of an impudent prostitute;

7578.text: in that you build your vaulted place at the head of every way, and make your lofty place in every street, and have not been as a prostitute, in that you scorn pay.

7579.text: "'A wife who commits adultery! who takes strangers instead of her husband!

7580.text: They give gifts to all prostitutes; but you give your gifts to all your lovers, and bribe them, that they may come to you on every side for your prostitution.

7581.text: You are different from other women in your prostitution, in that no one follows you to play the prostitute; and whereas you give hire, and no hire is given to you, therefore you are different.'

7582.text: "Therefore, prostitute, hear the word of the Lord:

7583.text: Thus says the Lord God, 'Because your filthiness was poured out, and your nakedness uncovered through your prostitution with your lovers; and because of all the idols of your abominations, and for the blood of your children, that you gave to them;

7584.text: therefore see, I will gather all your lovers, with whom you have taken pleasure, and all those who you have loved, with all those who you have hated; I will even gather them against you on every side, and will uncover your nakedness to them, that they may see all your nakedness.

7585.text: I will judge you, as women who break wedlock and shed blood are judged; and I will bring on you the blood of wrath and jealousy.

7586.text: I will also give you into their hand, and they shall throw down your vaulted place, and break down your lofty places; and they shall strip you of your clothes, and take your beautiful jewels; and they shall leave you naked and bare.

7587.text: They shall also bring up a company against you, and they shall stone you with stones, and thrust you through with their swords.

7588.text: They shall burn your houses with fire, and execute judgments on you in the sight of many women; and I will cause you to cease from playing the prostitute, and you shall also give no hire any more.

7589.text: So will I cause my wrath toward you to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from you, and I will be quiet, and will be no more angry.

7590.text: "'Because you have not remembered the days of your youth, but have raged against me in all these things; therefore, behold, I also will bring your way on your head,' says the Lord God: 'and you shall not commit this lewdness with all your abominations.

7591.text: "'Behold, everyone who uses proverbs shall use this proverb against you, saying, "As is the mother, so is her daughter."

7592.text: You are the daughter of your mother, who loathes her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children: your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.

7593.text: Your elder sister is Samaria, who dwells at your left hand, she and her daughters; and your younger sister, who dwells at your right hand, is Sodom and her daughters.

7594.text: Yet have you not walked in their ways, nor done after their abominations; but, as if that were a very little thing, you were more corrupt than they in all your ways.

7595.text: As I live,' says the Lord God, 'Sodom your sister has not done, she nor her daughters, as you have done, you and your daughters.

7596.text: "'Behold, this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: pride, fullness of bread, and prosperous ease was in her and in her daughters; neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.

7597.text: They were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw good.

7598.text: Neither has Samaria committed half of your sins; but you have multiplied your abominations more than they, and have justified your sisters by all your abominations which you have done.

7599.text: You also, bear you your own shame, in that you have given judgment for your sisters; through your sins that you have committed more abominable than they, they are more righteous that you: yes, be also confounded, and bear your shame, in that you have justified your sisters.

7600.text: "'I will turn again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, and the captivity of your captives in their midst;

7601.text: that you may bear your own shame, and may be ashamed because of all that you have done, in that you are a comfort to them.

7602.text: Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, shall return to their former estate; and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former estate; and you and your daughters shall return to your former estate.

7603.text: For your sister Sodom was not mentioned by your mouth in the day of your pride,

7604.text: before your wickedness was uncovered, as at the time of the reproach of the daughters of Syria, and of all who are around her, the daughters of the Philistines, who do despite to you all around.

7605.text: You have borne your lewdness and your abominations, says the Lord.'

7606.text: "For thus says the Lord God: 'I will also deal with you as you have done, who have despised the oath in breaking the covenant.

7607.text: Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish to you an everlasting covenant.

7608.text: Then you shall remember your ways, and be ashamed, when you shall receive your sisters, your elder sisters and your younger; and I will give them to you for daughters, but not by your covenant.

7609.text: I will establish my covenant with you; and you shall know that I am the Lord;

7610.text: that you may remember, and be confounded, and never open your mouth any more, because of your shame, when I have forgiven you all that you have done, says the Lord God.'"

7611.text: The word of the Lord came to me, saying,

7612.text: "Son of man, put forth a riddle, and speak a parable to the house of Israel;

7613.text: and say, 'Thus says the Lord God: "A great eagle with great wings and long feathers, full of feathers, which had various colors, came to Lebanon, and took the top of the cedar:

7614.text: he cropped off the topmost of the young twigs of it, and carried it to a land of traffic; he set it in a city of merchants.
